21	## 2026-06-01 Current Ask Answer
22	
23	The most elegant permanent solution is one relay-owned projection system for
24	every visible Codex Dock object. The system has one identity owner, one ordering
25	owner, one update ledger, one cache contract, one generated client contract, and
26	one proof witness source.
27	
28	The final architecture is:
29	
30	```text
31	raw Codex inputs
32	  -> relay source adapters
33	  -> pure projection engine
34	  -> versioned projection store
35	  -> projection view streams and witnesses
36	  -> Swift projection renderers
37	```
38	
39	No layer after the projection engine may answer "what visible row is this?"
40	again. Swift may render and validate. Proof may compare. SQLite may store. None
41	of them may derive production visible identity.
42	
43	This is the target pattern, not a narrow Thread Detail fix:
44	
45	1. One projection contract package defines the shared row envelope, snapshot
46	   envelope, update envelope, view parameters, typed payload schemas, and proof
47	   witness schemas.
48	2. The relay projection engine is the only production module allowed to create
49	   `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `rowRole`, `displayOrderKey`,
50	   `revision`, freshness, ledger operations, or diagnostic rows.
51	3. Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, Thread Detail, request rows,
52	   simulator UI proof, live-filter proof, sync audit, and fixture generation all
53	   consume that same projection package.
54	4. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
55	   notifications, and server requests stay as relay-internal source adapters.
56	   They are never phone-facing display contracts and never proof truth.
57	5. The app receives projection snapshots and updates only. It keys visible rows
58	   by relay `projectionID`, applies `snapshot` / `upsert` / `delete` /
59	   `heartbeat` / `resyncRequired` by `epoch` and `seq`, and sorts by
60	   `displayOrderKey`.
61	6. SQLite stores materialized projection rows and view memberships under the
62	   projection contract version. A contract bump invalidates old materialized
63	   rows before they can be served as fresh.
64	7. Request cards are projection rows with request payload. `requestID` is only
65	   the JSON-RPC response-routing token; it is not visible identity.
66	8. Local metadata, pins, filters, host settings, previews, and accessibility IDs
67	   decorate or expose projection rows. They never create a second row set,
68	   order, freshness state, or identity namespace.
69	9. Acceptance proof compares simulator accessibility dumps to relay-emitted
70	   projection witness envelopes from the same run. It does not reconstruct
71	   expected IDs from raw Codex data or imported ID helpers.
72	10. CI enforces the contract with schema generation/checking, strict proof
73	    schemas, forbidden side-door checks, and live temporal tests that exercise
74	    snapshots, updates, reconnects, resyncs, request resolution, and cache
75	    invalidation.
76	
77	Net: the architecture makes identity bugs go away by removing every second
78	identity owner. If a visible row exists, its identity came from the relay
79	projection engine or the row is invalid.
80	
81	## 2026-06-01 Current Repo Evidence
82	
83	This re-audit reads the dirty local worktree as evidence only. It does not mark
84	the worktree implementation complete.
85	
86	The repo is partially moved toward the target:
87

140	## Non-Negotiable Elegance Test
141	
142	This architecture is accepted only if the answer to each question is "one":
143	
144	- How many modules create production visible IDs? One relay projection engine.
145	- How many wire grammars update visible rows? One projection stream grammar.
146	- How many durable stores can serve visible projection rows as fresh? One
147	  versioned projection store.
148	- How many proof witnesses can define expected visible state? One retained
149	  relay projection witness from the same run.
150	- How many Swift display paths consume raw Codex history or live payloads? Zero.
151	- How many test helpers are allowed to predict production projection IDs beside
152	  the relay? Zero for acceptance proof; unit tests may call the projection
153	  package itself, not reimplement it.
154	
155	Anything else is not elegant; it is a second source of truth with nicer names.
156	
157	## Composer Tightening Incorporated
158	
159	The 2026-06-01 Composer 2.5 Fast consult agreed with the architecture and found
160	no blocking design gap. It did identify five places where the doc needed to be
161	more normative before implementation. This section is the incorporated answer.
162	
163	Request rows have one final rule:
164	
165	- If a server request has proven `turnID` + `itemID` and maps to a supported
166	  visible item row, the request state attaches to that item row's
167	  `projectionID`. The relay upserts the same row when canonical history catches
168	  up.
169	- If a server request lacks a usable item link, or the item link maps to an
170	  unsupported item role, the relay emits a standalone request row:
171	  `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request` or,
172	  when useful for diagnostics,
173	  `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/request:<requestID>/row:request`.
174	- The relay must never emit both an item row and a separate request row for the
175	  same proven request/item relationship. Request status is `revision` and
176	  payload state on the chosen `projectionID`, not another row identity.
177	
178	Projection witness export has one final rule:
179	
180	- The witness is a retained byte-for-byte copy of projection envelopes after
181	  the relay has emitted them to the downstream client path.
182	- The witness route may filter or redact non-identity payload fields for safe
183	  reporting, but it must not recompute `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`,
184	  membership, freshness, route counts, or expected UI rows.
185	- If the retained witness is missing, stale, malformed, or for a different
186	  `proofRunID`, proof is `blocked` or `fail`. It must not fall back to raw
187	  Codex reads, SQLite reconstruction, fixture helpers, or `projectionIDFor*`
188	  imports.
189	
190	Phase 1 is a hard architecture gate:
191	
192	- `contract/projection/**` must exist before any cutover is called complete.
193	- Node DTOs, Swift DTOs, fixtures, and proof schemas must be generated from or
194	  checked against that package.
195	- `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` can remain only as migration
196	  history or be moved into the projection package. It cannot remain a second
197	  production display schema.
198	
199	Swift render adapters have one final rule:
200	
201	- A Swift type named `ThreadEvent` may exist only as a projection-row render
202	  adapter keyed by relay `projectionID`.
203	- Production Thread Detail, Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, and Host Registry
204	  render state must reject missing `displayOrderKey` instead of falling back to
205	  local date/turn/item/event sorting.
206	- Fallback sorting is allowed only in quarantined legacy tests that prove the
207	  old path has been retired; it is not allowed in production display stores or
208	  acceptance proof.
209	
210	Enforcement is part of the architecture:
211	
212	- Forbidden-pattern gates are not lint polish. They are the mechanism that
213	  keeps the architecture from drifting back into multiple identity owners.
214	- No implementation can be accepted while production display code or acceptance
215	  proof still contains raw display routes, fixture-computed expected IDs,
216	  permissive proof schemas, `logicalHostID::threadID` identity, `baseSeq`,
217	  `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, `visibleEventIDs`, or request-card display
218	  IDs derived from `requestID`.
219	
220	## Architecture Decision
221	
222	The permanent answer is not "fix one duplicate." The permanent answer is a
223	single product projection plane:
224	
225	```text
226	raw Codex adapters -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection store -> view streams -> Swift renderers
227	```
228	
229	Only the relay projection engine answers these questions:
230	
231	- What visible thing is this?
232	- What is its stable identity?
233	- What source fact produced it?
234	- What order should it render in?
235	- Is it fresh, stale, partial, or diagnostic?
236	
237	Every production screen then consumes projection rows. Dock, Archive, Thread
238	Detail, request cards, simulator proof, and UI dump comparison all use the same
239	projection grammar. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
240	`thread/resume`, live notifications, and server requests become private input
241	adapters. They are not display contracts.
242	
243	This is intentionally zero-sunk-cost. If an existing route, DTO, SQLite table,
244	test fixture, or proof script lets another layer infer visible identity, it is
245	not preserved for convenience. It is deleted, quarantined as a non-production
246	diagnostic, or rewritten to consume projection rows.
247	
248	## Acceptance Standard
249	
250	The architecture is accepted only when all of these are true:
251	
252	- One schema source defines the shared projection envelope and typed view
253	  payloads.
254	- Node and Swift consume generated or schema-checked DTOs from that source.
255	- The relay has one pure projection engine for identity, source refs, order,
256	  freshness, and ledger operations.
257	- Dock and Archive cards are projection rows, not a separate `logicalHostID` /
258	  `host::thread` card grammar.
259	- Thread Detail messages and request cards are projection rows, not raw Codex
260	  rows normalized in Swift.
261	- Relay SQLite stores materialized projections keyed by projection contract
262	  version, source host, view membership, and projection identity.
263	- A projection contract version bump invalidates old materialized rows before
264	  they can be served as fresh.
265	- Swift display stores apply only projection snapshots and updates by
266	  `epoch`, `seq`, `projectionID`, and `displayOrderKey`.
267	- Swift never creates production visible IDs from raw Codex JSON, body text,
268	  timestamps, local UUIDs, WebSocket request IDs alone, or UI object lifetime.
269	- Proof scripts compare simulator accessibility state against relay projection
270	  snapshots or updates, not against a second reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
271	  Fields such as `expectedMessageEventIDs` are forbidden in acceptance proof
272	  outputs because they encode a second identity oracle.
273	- Test fixtures either come from the projection engine or validate against the
274	  projection schema. They do not invent production message/card IDs, and they
275	  do not compute expected UI IDs outside the relay-emitted projection ledger.
276	- Raw routes may exist only as relay-internal adapters, mutation routes, or
277	  named diagnostics. They cannot feed production display state or acceptance
278	  proof.
279	
280	Net: after implementation, identity drift is not a category of app bug because
281	there is no second production identity owner left.
282	
283	## Zero-Sunk-Cost Permanent Solution
284	
285	The objectively clean architecture is a projection system, not a Thread Detail
286	fix.
287	
288	The relay owns a single projection contract package. Raw Codex facts enter that
289	package; versioned projection rows leave it. Every user-visible Dock object is
290	then just a row in a projection view.
291	
292	The architecture has seven laws:
293	
294	1. Raw Codex routes are adapters only.
295	   `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
296	   notifications, and server requests may feed the relay, but they never define
297	   phone display identity.
298	2. One pure projection engine owns identity.
299	   The only production helpers that can create `sourceRef`, `projectionID`,
300	   `displayOrderKey`, row role, freshness, `identityVersion`, or
301	   `projectionEngineVersion` live in the relay projection contract package.
302	3. One ledger model owns updates.
303	   Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, and Thread Detail all use the
304	   same `snapshot`, `upsert`, `delete`, `heartbeat`, and `resyncRequired`
305	   semantics with `epoch`, `seq`, `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`, and
306	   `viewParamsKey`.
307	4. Swift is a renderer and validator.
308	   Swift decodes generated or schema-checked projection DTOs, validates the
309	   envelope, rejects gaps/mismatches, renders by `projectionID`, and sorts by
310	   `displayOrderKey`. It does not reconstruct visible identity from raw JSON,
311	   body text, timestamps, request IDs, UUIDs, or object lifetime.
312	5. `requestID` is never display identity.
313	   JSON-RPC `requestID` routes a response. If a request is visible, the visible
314	   row is still keyed by relay `projectionID`; request state is payload/revision.
315	6. Cache validity is part of the identity contract.
316	   Materialized rows are keyed by
317	   `schemaVersion + identityVersion + projectionEngineVersion + sourceHostID +
318	   view + viewParamsKey + projectionID`. A version bump cannot serve old rows as
319	   fresh.
320	7. Proof reads the emitted projection stream.
321	   Simulator/UI proof, live-filter proof, controlled fixtures, and acceptance
322	   reports compare the app only to relay-emitted projection snapshots/updates or
323	   a byte-for-byte retained witness export. They do not call `projectionIDFor*`
324	   helpers or reconstruct expected visible IDs beside the system under test.
325	
326	That is the elegance test. There can be many raw inputs and many screens, but
327	there is one place where a visible object becomes a visible object. If a future
328	feature cannot go through that place, the feature is architecturally incomplete.
329	
330	This deliberately rejects the cheaper alternatives:
331	
332	- no Swift-side duplicate suppression;
333	- no body-text dedupe;
334	- no "prefer newest route" heuristic;
335	- no second identity helper in tests;
336	- no keeping raw routes as hidden display proof paths;
337	- no accepting stale cache rows because they are "compatible enough."
338	
339	The end state is simple: the iPhone renders a projection view, and every row on
340	screen has exactly one relay projection identity.
341	
342	## User-Visible Bug
343	
344	When an outbound user message is sent, Thread Detail can show that outbound
345	message twice.
346	
347	The intended behavior is simpler:
348	
349	- One user send produces one visible user-message row.
350	- That row may move or lose its live badge as canonical history catches up.
351	- It must not remain as both a live row and a canonical row.
352	
353	## Root Cause
354	
355	The original pre-projection Thread Detail path had no single canonical event
356	identity layer for "the same Codex item" across live notifications and
357	canonical history reads.
358	
359	That client path stored `ThreadEvent` rows in `ThreadEventIndex` and merged
360	only by:
361	
362	1. Exact `ThreadEvent.id`.
363	2. A secondary stream key of `turnID + itemID + kind + visibility`.
364	
365	That works only when every producer gives the same `turnID` and `itemID` in the
366	same place. The outbound path does not guarantee that.
367	
368	The dangerous path is:
369	
370	1. Thread Detail is live through `thread/resume`.
371	2. A user sends or otherwise creates a user message.
372	3. The live session can emit an `item/started` or `item/completed` notification.
373	4. The app turns that live notification into a `ThreadEvent`.
374	5. The Dock row updates, so Thread Detail does a canonical reread:
375	   `thread/read` + all pages of `thread/turns/list` + `thread/resume`.
376	6. That canonical reread is merged into the existing event index, not used as a
377	   replacement.
378	7. If the live row and canonical row do not normalize to the same event identity,
379	   both survive and render as two visible user-message cards.
380	
381	That was a client-side merge contract bug. The current work-in-progress moves
382	the direct Thread Detail display path toward relay projection DTOs, but the
383	broader architecture is not complete until all display surfaces and proof paths
384	share the same projection identity plane.
385	
386	## What This Is Not
387	
388	This does not look like a SwiftUI `ForEach` rendering duplicate. `ForEach` keys
389	rows by `ThreadEventRenderRow.id`, which is `event.id`.
390	
391	This does not look like an optimistic-send duplicate. `ThreadDetailStore.sendDraft`
392	does not add a local pending message row. It sends `turn/start` or `turn/steer`,
393	then clears the draft and updates `activeTurnID`.
394	
395	This does not look like a relay "sent the same command twice" bug from the code
396	path alone. The relay forwards `turn/start` and `turn/steer` to the active
397	upstream after checking that the downstream detail session is bound to the same
398	thread. It does not create Thread Detail rows.
399	
400	The duplicate is produced after the client accepts multiple representations of
401	the same logical Codex item and fails to collapse them.
402	
403	## Original Pre-Projection Code Touchpoints

451	`CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift`

453	When the Dock row updates, Thread Detail queues a refresh:

468	### Event Identity Path
469	
470	`CodexDock/Models/ThreadEvent.swift`
471	
472	Stored canonical history:

480	- `event(from notification:)` handles `item/started` and `item/completed`.
481	- It passes `params["item"]` into the same `events(fromItem:)` helper, with the
482	  top-level notification params as `turn`.
483	- `events(fromItem:)` only reads `object["id"]` from the nested item object.

497	## Why The Existing Tests Miss This
498	
499	The tests prove pieces, but not the failure path.
500	
501	Current coverage:
502	
503	- `ThreadDetailStoreTests.testSendDraftStartsTurnWhenNoActiveTurnAndClearsDraft`
504	  proves `turn/start` is called and the draft clears.
505	- `ThreadDetailStoreTests.testSendDraftSteersKnownActiveTurn` proves
506	  `turn/steer` is called for an active turn.
507	- `ThreadDetailStreamingMergeTests.testCompletedAgentMessageReplacesLiveDeltaInsteadOfDuplicating`
508	  proves an agent delta and an agent completed item merge when both paths use
509	  the same nested item ID.
510	
511	Missing coverage:
512	
513	- No test sends a draft and then emits the live user-message notification that
514	  Codex sends back.
515	- No test follows that with the Dock-row-triggered canonical reread.
516	- No test asserts "same outbound user body appears exactly once" after live
517	  event plus canonical reread.
518	- No test covers live full-item notifications where identity appears in a
519	  different place than stored history.
520	- No simulator proof currently drives the real composer send path and then
521	  checks Thread Detail visible message-card IDs for duplicates.

523	That is why the current tests can pass while the phone shows a duplicated
524	outbound message.

550	## Why The Quick Fallback Fix Was Not Good Enough
551	
552	The reverted idea was to make `item/started` and `item/completed` use top-level
553	`params["itemId"]` when nested `item.id` is missing.
554	
555	That may be part of the eventual fix, but by itself it is too narrow because it
556	does not establish a single rule for Thread Detail identity. It patches one
557	shape instead of defining the contract.
558	
559	The correct fix should define one canonical event identity function and route
560	all event producers through it:
561	
562	- stored turn item from `thread/turns/list`
563	- live streaming delta from `item/*/delta`
564	- live full item from `item/started` and `item/completed`
565	- server request rows
566	- canonical reread merge rows
567	
568	The merge layer should then merge by that canonical identity, not by whatever
569	ad hoc `ThreadEvent.id` each producer happens to build.
570	
571	## Permanent Architecture Proposal
572	
573	The earlier narrow answer was "put Thread Detail row identity in the relay."
574	That is directionally right, but it is not the full permanent answer if the bar
575	is "this whole class of identity issues stops being a concern."
576	
577	The full answer is one relay-owned projection identity plane for every
578	user-visible Dock object:
579	
580	```text
581	raw Codex state -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection ledger -> Swift renderer
582	```
583	
584	Swift, UI proof scripts, simulator fixtures, and tests should never separately
585	decide what a visible production row/card "is." They can render, validate, and
586	compare projection rows, but they do not own production identity.
587	
588	This is a stronger architecture than a Thread Detail-only patch because the
589	same failure shape has already appeared in several forms:
590	
591	- Dock cards were ordered from stale thread-level metadata while newer turn
592	  state existed somewhere else.
593	- Thread Detail could merge live and canonical rows under different IDs.
594	- Request cards had their own card/request identity beside message rows.
595	- Proof scripts reconstructed expected UI IDs instead of reading the relay's
596	  display ledger.
597	- Tests used fake/static snapshots that did not exercise real temporal
598	  convergence.
599	
600	The permanent fix is therefore not "normalize one more payload field." The
601	permanent fix is to make visible identity, visible order, freshness, and update
602	continuity a single projection contract at the relay boundary.

703	### The Object Model
704	
705	Use three separate concepts everywhere. Mixing them is what creates duplicates:
706	
707	| Concept | Owner | Meaning | May change? |
708	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
709	| `sourceRef` | Relay normalizer | Stable reference to the raw Codex fact, including host/thread/turn/item/request identity. | No, unless the relay emits a supersession from pending to canonical. |
710	| `projectionID` | Relay normalizer | Stable visible row/card identity derived from `sourceRef` plus row role. | No. |
711	| `revision` | Relay ledger | Version of the content for the same `projectionID`. | Yes. |
712	
713	The renderer keys UI rows by `projectionID`. Content changes, streaming text,
714	request status changes, and canonical catch-up updates bump `revision`; they do
715	not create new row identity.
716	
717	The canonical identity namespace should include host identity, not just
718	`threadID`, so two relays or two Codex homes cannot collide:
719	
720	```text
721	host:<sourceHostID>/row:host
722	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
723	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<rowRole>
724	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
725	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/system:<systemKind>/<stableSourceSequence>
726	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/diagnostic:<stableHash>/row:unknown
727	```
728	
729	Dock and Archive use the same thread-card identity:
730	
731	```text
732	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
733	```
734	
735	The route `view` decides whether that row appears in Dock or Archive. Archive
736	state is payload state, not a separate card identity. The Dock/Archive card
737	`sourceRef` is:
738	
739	```text
740	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>
741	```
742	
743	The existing Dock `logicalHostID` field is a transition alias for
744	`sourceHostID`; if a payload
745	carries both and they disagree, the relay must diagnose or resync instead of
746	letting Swift choose.
747	
748	`sourceHostID` is the relay's canonical identity for the Codex source host. It
749	must be stable across Bonjour name changes, LAN/Tailscale endpoint changes, and
750	phone saved host config edits. UI labels can change; source identity cannot.
751	
752	The derivation rule is:
753	
754	1. Use non-empty `CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID` from relay-side configuration.
755	2. Else use the persisted value in `.codex-dock/source-host-id`.
756	3. Else create `.codex-dock/source-host-id` once as
757	   `local-<sha256(platform + user + CODEX_HOME + historyUrl)[0..12]>`.
758	
759	`sourceHostID` must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`. It must not be
760	derived from endpoint hostnames, Bonjour names, LAN IPs, Tailscale names, saved
761	phone host config, WebSocket connection IDs, relay process IDs, or
762	`CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_INSTANCE_ID`.
763	
764	### Projection Row Envelope
765	
766	Every user-visible projection row should share one envelope, even when the row
767	payload is typed differently for Dock cards, Archive cards, Thread Detail
768	messages, and request cards:
769	
770	```json
771	{
772	  "schemaVersion": 1,
773	  "identityVersion": 1,
774	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
775	  "view": "thread.detail",
776	  "threadID": "019e...",
777	  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1/row:userMessage",
778	  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1",
779	  "rowRole": "userMessage",
780	  "revision": 7,
781	  "displayOrderKey": "9998239345599999|0000000000|9999999999|9999999999|...",
782	  "freshness": {
783	    "state": "fresh",
784	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
785	  },
786	  "payload": {}
787	}
788	```
789	
790	The row-specific payload can stay typed:
791	
792	- Dock and Archive rows carry card fields.
793	- Thread Detail rows carry message/request/system fields.
794	- Request-backed rows carry `requestID` for responses, but the visible row key
795	  remains `projectionID`.
796	
797	The shared envelope is what kills identity drift. The screen can vary; the
798	identity and update rules do not.

800	### Projection Snapshot And Update Envelope
801	
802	Each subscribed view should use the same stream grammar:
803	
804	```json
805	{
806	  "schemaVersion": 1,
807	  "identityVersion": 1,
808	  "view": "thread.detail",
809	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
810	  "threadID": "019e...",
811	  "epoch": "projection-...",
812	  "seq": 42,
813	  "scope": "thread",
814	  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
815	  "complete": true,
816	  "freshness": {
817	    "state": "fresh",
818	    "asOf": "2026-06-01T18:00:00.000Z",
819	    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
820	  },
821	  "rows": []
822	}
823	```
824	
825	Updates are only:
826	
827	- `snapshot`: replace the declared scope.
828	- `upsert`: insert or replace rows by `projectionID`.
829	- `delete`: remove rows by `projectionID`.
830	- `heartbeat`: prove continuity without changing rows.
831	- `resyncRequired`: declare continuity broken and force a replacement
832	  snapshot.
833	
834	Every update carries `epoch` and `seq`. Swift applies only the active epoch and
835	monotonic sequence. A new epoch without a snapshot is invalid. A sequence gap is
836	not "probably fine"; it is stale until resync succeeds.
837	
838	Every projection snapshot and update also carries `projectionEngineVersion`.
839	Clients store the active engine version with the active epoch. If an update
840	arrives with a different `projectionEngineVersion` inside the same epoch, the
841	client rejects it and requests the matching resync route. A new engine version
842	is accepted only through a replacement snapshot with a new epoch.
843	
844	`projectionEngineVersion` is required on every projection snapshot and update
845	envelope for Dock, Archive, Host Registry, and Thread Detail. Stored projection
846	rows also carry the engine version as cache metadata. If Swift sees an engine
847	version mismatch, it must not translate old rows locally; it marks the view
848	stale and asks the relay for a replacement snapshot.
849	
850	The existing route names can remain because they are understandable:
851	
852	- `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`
853	- `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, `archive/resync`
854	- `thread/detail/read`, `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
855	  `thread/detail/resync`
856	
857	The elegant part is not a single generic route name. The elegant part is that
858	all three route families obey the same projection envelope and identity rules.
859	
860	### Cross-View Scope And Snapshot Authority
861	
862	Thread Detail already names `scope: "thread"` and optional `scope: "window"`.
863	Dock and Archive need the same explicit authority rule so card cutover does not
864	recreate merge ambiguity under new names.
865	
866	Accepted projection scopes:
867	
868	| View | Scope | Meaning | Snapshot replacement rule |
869	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
870	| `dock` | `view` | Complete active Dock view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `dock` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
871	| `archive` | `view` | Complete Archive view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `archive` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
872	| `archive.cleanup` | `view` | Complete Archive Cleanup candidate view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local cleanup candidate row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
873	| `dock` | `host` | Complete active Dock view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
874	| `archive` | `host` | Complete Archive view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
875	| `archive.cleanup` | `host` | Complete cleanup candidate view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only cleanup rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
876	| `dock` / `archive` / `archive.cleanup` | `window` | Bounded key range inside a card-like view. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |
877	| `host.registry` | `view` | Complete host registry for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local host row for that registry view with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
878	| `thread.detail` | `thread` | Complete detail view for one thread. | Replace every local row for that `sourceHostID`, `threadID`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
879	| `thread.detail` | `window` | Bounded key range inside one thread. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |
880	
881	Dock and Archive stream envelopes omit `threadID` at the snapshot/update
882	envelope level unless the update is explicitly scoped to one thread. Card rows
883	carry `payload.threadID` and, when useful for validation, an envelope
884	`threadID`. Swift must not infer a Dock/Archive snapshot's authority from the
885	presence or absence of row IDs; it uses `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`,
886	`viewParamsKey`, and window bounds.
887	
888	For every view:
889	
890	- `snapshot` with `scope: "view"` or `scope: "host"` is authoritative for its
891	  declared scope.
892	- `snapshot` with `scope: "window"` is authoritative only for the declared
893	  order-key range.
894	- `upsert` inserts or replaces exact `projectionID`s.
895	- `delete` removes exact `projectionID`s.
896	- `heartbeat` proves continuity only; it never changes membership.
897	- `resyncRequired` makes the active view stale until the matching resync route
898	  returns a replacement snapshot.

993	  16 decimal digits.
994	- `statusPriority` is left-padded to 4 decimal digits and is relay-owned:
995	  needs-approval/user-input before running before idle before error before
996	  unknown/dormant when activity ties exactly.
997	- `safeProjectionID` is the canonical escaped `projectionID` tie breaker.
998	- Swift compares the full string only; it never parses it back into fields.
999	
1000	Normative `statusPriority` values:
1001	
1002	| Card status | Priority |
1003	| --- | --- |
1004	| `needsInput` | `0000` |
1005	| `needsApproval` | `0000` |
1006	| `running` | `0001` |
1007	| `idle` | `0002` |
1008	| `error` | `0003` |
1009	| `unknown` | `0004` |
1010	| any unrecognized active status | `0004` |
1011	| `dormant` / not loaded | `0005` |
1012	
1013	### Archive Cleanup Projection View
1014	
1015	Archive Cleanup is its own relay-projected view:
1016	
1017	```text
1018	view: "archive.cleanup"
1019	```
1020	
1021	Routes:
1022	
1023	- `archive/cleanup/read`
1024	- `archive/cleanup/subscribe`
1025	- `archive/cleanup/update`
1026	- `archive/cleanup/resync`
1027	
1028	Archive Cleanup rows use the same `threadCard` row payload and the same card
1029	`projectionID` as Dock and Archive:
1030	
1031	```text
1032	host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
1033	```
1034	
1035	Cleanup membership is view membership, not row identity. The cleanup view
1036	selects active cleanup candidates through relay-owned `viewParams`:
1037	
1038	```json
1039	{
1040	  "viewParams": {
1041	    "candidateSource": "activeDock",
1042	    "hostIDs": null,
1043	    "statusKinds": null,
1044	    "olderThan": null,
1045	    "repositorySearch": "",
1046	    "branchSearch": "",
1047	    "textSearch": "",
1048	    "includeDiagnostics": true,
1049	    "sort": "displayOrderKeyAscending"
1050	  }
1051	}
1052	```
1053	
1054	`viewParamsKey` is required on every Archive Cleanup snapshot/update. Proof for
1055	Archive Cleanup compares simulator UI to `view: "archive.cleanup"` witness
1056	envelopes with the same `viewParamsKey`. It never treats a raw Dock stream or a
1057	client-filtered Dock list as cleanup truth.
1058	
1059	### Host Projection Rows
1060	
1061	`host:<sourceHostID>/row:host` is a real projection row, not decorative
1062	metadata. It exists so host identity, labels, connectivity summaries, and proof
1063	state have the same identity law as thread cards and detail rows.
1064	
1065	Host row envelope:
1066	
1067	```json
1068	{
1069	  "schemaVersion": 1,
1070	  "identityVersion": 1,
1071	  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
1072	  "view": "host.registry",
1073	  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/row:host",
1074	  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5",
1075	  "rowRole": "host",
1076	  "revision": 3,
1077	  "displayOrderKey": "host|amir-m5",
1078	  "freshness": {
1079	    "state": "fresh"
1080	  },
1081	  "payload": {
1082	    "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
1083	    "displayName": "Amir M5",
1084	    "endpointLabels": ["amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510"],
1085	    "connectivityState": "online",
1086	    "lastContactAt": "2026-06-01T19:50:00.000Z"
1087	  }
1088	}
1089	```
1090	
1091	Rules:
1092	
1093	- host rows are keyed only by `sourceHostID`.
1094	- endpoint, Bonjour, LAN, Tailscale, and saved-phone labels are payload labels,
1095	  never identity.
1096	- phone saved host configs are bootstrap connection records only. They may have
1097	  local config IDs for settings UI, but those IDs never appear in
1098	  `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`, or proof
1099	  witnesses.
1100	- host row ordering is stable label order unless a future host view defines a
1101	  relay-owned `displayOrderKey`.
1102	- thread-card rows reference the host row through `sourceHostID`; they do not
1103	  embed a second host identity namespace.
1104	
1105	Host Registry routes use the same projection grammar:
1106	
1107	- `host/registry/read`
1108	- `host/registry/subscribe`
1109	- `host/registry/update`
1110	- `host/registry/resync`
1111	
1112	`HostRegistrySnapshotDTO` and `HostRegistryUpdateDTO` are the same shared
1113	snapshot/update envelopes with `view: "host.registry"` and host-row payloads.
1114	If the app shows configured endpoints before a relay connection exists, that is
1115	settings UI backed by phone config, not a projection view and not evidence of
1116	Codex source identity. Once connected, any user-visible Codex source identity,
1117	label, connectivity summary, or proof state comes from host projection rows.
1118	
1119	### Identity Law
1120	
1121	These are architectural laws, not implementation suggestions:
1122	
1123	1. No production visible row/card ID may be generated from body text, timestamp,
1124	   list offset alone, local UI state, Swift object lifetime, WebSocket request
1125	   ID alone, `UUID()`, or `crypto.randomUUID()`.
1126	2. A supported raw Codex item without enough identity does not become a normal
1127	   message row. It becomes a stable diagnostic row or a `resyncRequired` update.
1128	3. Live, history, reconnect, canonical reread, server request, request
1129	   resolution, and proof paths all call the same relay projection normalizer.
1130	4. Streaming and settled forms of one Codex item share one `projectionID`.
1131	5. Request controls are attached to the same `projectionID` as their visible
1132	   row. `requestID` is only the response routing key.
1133	6. Sorting is by relay `displayOrderKey` only. Swift does not rebuild newest
1134	   ordering from raw timestamps or turn/item indexes.
1135	7. Local metadata can decorate projection rows, but it cannot create production
1136	   rows or override projection identity/order/freshness.
1137	8. Diagnostics and health routes can explain state, but cannot be accepted as
1138	   data truth for the UI.
1139	9. Test fixtures must use projection DTOs or the relay normalizer. A fake that
1140	   invents message IDs is testing a different product.
1141	10. Proof scripts must compare UI state against relay projection snapshots or
1142	    updates, not against a second reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
1143	11. Acceptance proof cannot contain `expectedMessageEventIDs`, fixture-computed
1144	    visible IDs, or any other expected-ID list that was not emitted by the relay
1145	    projection ledger.
1146	12. Local metadata, including pin, hide, archive, and user filter state, may
1147	    request a relay view or decorate returned rows. It cannot change the row set
1148	    used by acceptance proof outside the relay projection view being proved.
1149	
1150	Pin and local metadata rule: cached pinned/local display snapshots are never
1151	authoritative after projection cutover. A pin can render chrome on an existing
1152	projection row, or a future relay-owned pinned view can be added with explicit
1153	`viewParamsKey` and witness proof. Swift cannot use local pin state to create a
1154	second row order, second membership set, or alternate cache of projection rows.
1155	
1156	### Relay Projection Engine
1157	
1158	The relay should have one pure projection engine that is independent from
1159	WebSockets, timers, SQLite, and Swift:
1160	
1161	```text
1162	normalizeRawCodexSource(rawSource, context) -> ProjectionRow[]
1163	applyProjectionOperation(ledger, operation) -> ledger
1164	projectDockView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<DockCard>
1165	projectArchiveView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<DockCard>
1166	projectHostRegistryView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<HostRow>
1167	projectThreadDetailView(ledger, scope) -> ProjectionSnapshot<ThreadDetailRow>
1168	```
1169	
1170	That engine has one production module, not one module per screen. The target
1171	module is:
1172	
1173	```text
1174	scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs
1175	```
1176	
1177	All production helpers named like `projectionIDFor*`, `sourceRefFor*`,
1178	`displayOrderKeyFor*`, and row-role mappers live there or under that module's
1179	owned package directory. View-specific relay files such as Thread Detail
1180	ledger, Dock state, Archive state, Archive Cleanup, and simulator fixtures may
1181	call the engine; they must not define their own visible identity grammar. Tests
1182	may import the pure engine for unit coverage, but acceptance proof cannot use
1183	that import as its expected-ID oracle. Acceptance proof reads IDs from emitted
1184	projection envelopes only.
1185	
1186	Runtime code does I/O:
1187	
1188	- read raw app-server state.
1189	- maintain upstream live sessions.
1190	- receive server requests.
1191	- write/read SQLite projection state.
1192	- publish downstream JSON-RPC snapshots and updates.
1193	
1194	The projection engine does identity, role mapping, order keys, freshness, and
1195	ledger operations. It has no socket state and no UI state. That is what makes
1196	it testable and prevents "one more path" from becoming another identity owner.
1197	
1198	### Reference Architecture Components
1199	
1200	The clean permanent architecture has these components and only these
1201	responsibilities:
1202	
1203	| Component | Owns | Must not own |
1204	| --- | --- | --- |
1205	| Raw Codex adapters | Fetching and subscribing to raw upstream state: `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live notifications, server requests. | Visible identity, UI order, freshness labels, or Swift DTO shape. |
1206	| Source host identity provider | Stable `sourceHostID` for the Codex source. | Endpoint labels, relay process identity, phone host config, or display names. |
1207	| Projection engine | `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `rowRole`, `displayOrderKey`, freshness, diagnostics, and ledger operations. | WebSocket lifecycle, SQLite I/O, Swift rendering, or test-only shortcuts. |
1208	| Projection store | Materialized projection rows, view memberships, epochs, sequence numbers, and cache contract versions. | Raw Codex as durable truth or screen-specific identity grammars. |
1209	| View stream routers | `dock/*`, `archive/*`, `archive/cleanup/*`, `host/registry/*`, `thread/detail/*` snapshots, updates, heartbeats, and resyncs over JSON-RPC. | Recomputing row identity or order. |
1210	| Swift projection stores | Applying projection snapshots/updates and publishing render state. | Parsing raw Codex display rows, recovering missing identity, or fallback sorting. |
1211	| Phone saved host config | Bootstrap endpoint list used to connect to relays. | `sourceHostID`, `projectionID`, host row identity, or freshness proof. |
1212	| UI and automation | Rendering projection rows and exposing `projectionID`-based accessibility IDs. | Creating production row IDs. |
1213	| Proof tools | Comparing UI dumps to relay projection snapshots/updates. | Building a second raw Codex oracle for display identity. |
1214	
1215	The projection store should not be three unrelated caches. Use one canonical
1216	projection storage model:
1217	
1218	```text
1219	projection_contracts
1220	  sourceHostID
1221	  schemaVersion
1222	  identityVersion
1223	  projectionEngineVersion
1224	  createdAt
1225	
1226	projection_rows
1227	  sourceHostID
1228	  projectionID
1229	  sourceRef
1230	  rowRole
1231	  revision
1232	  displayOrderKey
1233	  freshness
1234	  payloadJSON
1235	  updatedAt
1236	
1237	projection_view_memberships
1238	  sourceHostID
1239	  view
1240	  scope
1241	  projectionID
1242	  membershipState
1243	  displayOrderKey
1244	
1245	projection_stream_epochs
1246	  sourceHostID
1247	  view
1248	  scope
1249	  epoch
1250	  seq
1251	  complete
1252	  freshness
1253	```
1254	
1255	Dock active rows, Archive rows, and Thread Detail rows are all projection rows
1256	plus view membership. Moving a card from Dock to Archive changes membership or
1257	payload state; it does not invent a second card identity.
1258	
1259	The existing SQLite `threads` table can be migrated into this model or replaced
1260	outright. The elegant target is the universal model above because it removes
1261	screen-specific identity storage instead of teaching three tables the same
1262	rules.
1263	
1264	### Dock And Archive Migration Is Normative
1265	
1266	Dock and Archive are not allowed to stay on a parallel card stream grammar.
1267	They must move from the current card v2 stream to the shared projection stream.
1268	
1269	Current card v2 shape:
1270	
1271	```text
1272	kind: snapshot | delta | heartbeat
1273	id: <logicalHostID>::<threadID>
1274	logicalHostID
1275	stateGeneration
1276	cards / upsertCards / deleteCardIDs
1277	```
1278	
1279	Target projection shape:
1280	
1281	```text
1282	kind: snapshot | upsert | delete | heartbeat | resyncRequired
1283	projectionID: host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
1284	sourceHostID
1285	identityVersion
1286	projectionEngineVersion
1287	seq
1288	rows / projectionIDs
1289	```
1290	
1291	Normative mapping:
1292	
1293	| Current v2 field/concept | Target projection contract |
1294	| --- | --- |
1295	| `DockThreadCardDTO.id` | Removed as independent identity or transition-equal to `projectionID`; final identity is `projectionID`. |
1296	| `logicalHostID` | Payload alias only during migration; must validate one-to-one against `sourceHostID` and cannot appear in identity decisions. |
1297	| `delta` | Replaced by explicit `upsert` and `delete` operations. |
1298	| `upsertCards` | `rows` where each row has the shared projection envelope plus thread-card payload. |
1299	| `deleteCardIDs` | `projectionIDs`. |
1300	| `stateGeneration` | Removed; `epoch` and `seq` are the stream continuity contract. |
1301	| `baseSeq` | Removed unless the shared projection contract later adopts it for all views. Do not keep it Dock-only. |
1302	| `orderKey` | Replaced by `displayOrderKey`, opaque to Swift. |
1303	| `freshness.status` | Replaced by shared `freshness.state`; old names may exist only inside migration fixtures. |
1304	| archive membership | `projection_view_memberships`, not a second card identity. |
1305	
1306	Cutover rule:
1307	
1308	- A final implementation may use a temporary translation layer inside the relay,
1309	  but the phone-facing production route must emit the target projection shape
1310	  before acceptance.
1311	- `dock/subscribe`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`, and `archive/resync`
1312	  may keep their route names. Route names are transport. The payload grammar is
1313	  what must converge.
1314	- No Phase 7 pass is allowed while Swift display code, proof scripts, or schema
1315	  fixtures still accept card v2 `delta`/`logicalHostID::threadID` as production
1316	  display truth.
1317	- If a compatibility payload carries both `id` and `projectionID`, they must be
1318	  byte-for-byte equal or the client must reject the payload and request resync.
1319	
1320	### Contract Source Of Truth
1321	
1322	The contract source should be one schema/generator package, not hand-synced

# Codex Dock Thread Detail Outbound Duplicate Root Cause

Date: 2026-06-01

Status: local single-host implementation proof complete under the active
2026-06-01 goal; default two-host proof remains blocked until `home` is updated.
This doc began as the root-cause audit plus zero-sunk-cost permanent
architecture proposal for eliminating display identity drift as a class of
bugs. The architecture passed plan review, implementation audit, Composer 2.5
Fast fresh consult, thermonuclear maintainability review, and local-host
iPhone 17 simulator proof. Default two-host proof is not accepted yet because
`home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510` still needs the same relay deployment as
`amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`.

Related:

- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_LIVE_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_AND_TESTING_REFERENCE_2026-06-01.md`
- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md`
- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md`

## 2026-06-01 Current Ask Answer

The most elegant permanent solution is one relay-owned projection system for
every visible Codex Dock object. The system has one identity owner, one ordering
owner, one update ledger, one cache contract, one generated client contract, and
one proof witness source.

The final architecture is:

```text
raw Codex inputs
  -> relay source adapters
  -> pure projection engine
  -> versioned projection store
  -> projection view streams and witnesses
  -> Swift projection renderers
```

No layer after the projection engine may answer "what visible row is this?"
again. Swift may render and validate. Proof may compare. SQLite may store. None
of them may derive production visible identity.

This is the target pattern, not a narrow Thread Detail fix:

1. One projection contract package defines the shared row envelope, snapshot
   envelope, update envelope, view parameters, typed payload schemas, and proof
   witness schemas.
2. The relay projection engine is the only production module allowed to create
   `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`, `rowRole`, `displayOrderKey`,
   `revision`, freshness, ledger operations, or diagnostic rows.
3. Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, Thread Detail, request rows,
   simulator UI proof, live-filter proof, sync audit, and fixture generation all
   consume that same projection package.
4. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
   notifications, and server requests stay as relay-internal source adapters.
   They are never phone-facing display contracts and never proof truth.
5. The app receives projection snapshots and updates only. It keys visible rows
   by relay `projectionID`, applies `snapshot` / `upsert` / `delete` /
   `heartbeat` / `resyncRequired` by `epoch` and `seq`, and sorts by
   `displayOrderKey`.
6. SQLite stores materialized projection rows and view memberships under the
   projection contract version. A contract bump invalidates old materialized
   rows before they can be served as fresh.
7. Request cards are projection rows with request payload. `requestID` is only
   the JSON-RPC response-routing token; it is not visible identity.
8. Local metadata, pins, filters, host settings, previews, and accessibility IDs
   decorate or expose projection rows. They never create a second row set,
   order, freshness state, or identity namespace.
9. Acceptance proof compares simulator accessibility dumps to relay-emitted
   projection witness envelopes from the same run. It does not reconstruct
   expected IDs from raw Codex data or imported ID helpers.
10. CI enforces the contract with schema generation/checking, strict proof
    schemas, forbidden side-door checks, and live temporal tests that exercise
    snapshots, updates, reconnects, resyncs, request resolution, and cache
    invalidation.

Net: the architecture makes identity bugs go away by removing every second
identity owner. If a visible row exists, its identity came from the relay
projection engine or the row is invalid.

## 2026-06-01 Current Repo Evidence

This re-audit reads the dirty local worktree as evidence only. It does not mark
the worktree implementation complete.

The repo is partially moved toward the target:

- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift` now subscribes and resyncs through
  `thread/detail/subscribe` and `thread/detail/resync`.
- `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift` now applies Thread
  Detail projection rows by `projectionID`, `epoch`, and `seq`.
- `scripts/dock-relay-thread-detail-ledger.mjs` creates Thread Detail
  projection rows with `sourceHostID`, `sourceRef`, `projectionID`,
  `displayOrderKey`, and request payload.
- `scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs` is the seed of the right pure
  projection package.
- `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerClient.swift` now hides arbitrary
  `sendRequest(method:)` from public callers, which is the right direction.

The repo still has side doors that the final architecture must close:

- Dock and Archive still have card-shaped vocabulary and stores such as
  `cardsByID`, `DockThreadCardDTO`, `ThreadCardTable`, and card-specific
  fixture helpers. That can be a transition name only; final identity is
  `projectionID`.
- `DockRowViewModel.id` still carries `HostScopedThreadID`, so Dock/Archive UI
  actions still need a full cutover to projection identity plus explicit
  source/action payload.
- Relay proof and diagnostic scripts still contain old stream grammar markers:
  `baseSeq`, `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, `visibleEventIDs`,
  `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume` as proof-side
  vocabulary.
- `scripts/dock-relay-simulator-ui-sync-proof.mjs` and related tests still
  contain `.freshDock.cards`, local `projectionIDForThread` helpers, and legacy
  `expectedMessageProjectionIDs` fallback behavior.
- `scripts/codex-dock-live-filter-truth.mjs` and
  `scripts/codex-dock-live-filter-compare.mjs` still rebuild detail truth from
  raw `thread/turns/list` vocabulary and `visibleEventIDs`.
- Controlled simulator scripts still require raw `thread/read`,
  `thread/turns/list`, and `thread/resume` in several client-path proof
  scenarios. Those routes are allowed only as relay-internal upstream adapter
  calls, not as client proof routes.
- `CodexDockTests/LegacyThreadDetailRawDTOs.swift` and
  `CodexDockTests/LegacyThreadEventFixtureNormalizer.swift` quarantine legacy
  behavior in tests, but they are still a second expected-output oracle until
  projection fixtures are generated by the projection package.
- Proof schemas under `contract/proof` still use `additionalProperties: true`,
  so stale fields can pass unless semantic checks catch them. Final proof
  schemas must reject unknown identity and route fields by default.
- Request card display now derives from Thread Detail projection rows, with
  phone-only input/status state keyed by `projectionID`. `requestID` remains
  response routing only, not display identity.
- Raw upstream routes still correctly exist in `scripts/dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`
  and `scripts/dock-relay.mjs` as relay source adapters. The architecture must
  keep them there and forbid them everywhere else.

Those findings do not weaken the target architecture. They explain why the
target must be a package-and-contract cutover, not another local patch.

## Non-Negotiable Elegance Test

This architecture is accepted only if the answer to each question is "one":

- How many modules create production visible IDs? One relay projection engine.
- How many wire grammars update visible rows? One projection stream grammar.
- How many durable stores can serve visible projection rows as fresh? One
  versioned projection store.
- How many proof witnesses can define expected visible state? One retained
  relay projection witness from the same run.
- How many Swift display paths consume raw Codex history or live payloads? Zero.
- How many test helpers are allowed to predict production projection IDs beside
  the relay? Zero for acceptance proof; unit tests may call the projection
  package itself, not reimplement it.

Anything else is not elegant; it is a second source of truth with nicer names.

## Composer Tightening Incorporated

The 2026-06-01 Composer 2.5 Fast consult agreed with the architecture and found
no blocking design gap. It did identify five places where the doc needed to be
more normative before implementation. This section is the incorporated answer.

Request rows have one final rule:

- If a server request has proven `turnID` + `itemID` and maps to a supported
  visible item row, the request state attaches to that item row's
  `projectionID`. The relay upserts the same row when canonical history catches
  up.
- If a server request lacks a usable item link, or the item link maps to an
  unsupported item role, the relay emits a standalone request row:
  `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request` or,
  when useful for diagnostics,
  `host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/request:<requestID>/row:request`.
- The relay must never emit both an item row and a separate request row for the
  same proven request/item relationship. Request status is `revision` and
  payload state on the chosen `projectionID`, not another row identity.

Projection witness export has one final rule:

- The witness is a retained byte-for-byte copy of projection envelopes after
  the relay has emitted them to the downstream client path.
- The witness route may filter or redact non-identity payload fields for safe
  reporting, but it must not recompute `projectionID`, `displayOrderKey`,
  membership, freshness, route counts, or expected UI rows.
- If the retained witness is missing, stale, malformed, or for a different
  `proofRunID`, proof is `blocked` or `fail`. It must not fall back to raw
  Codex reads, SQLite reconstruction, fixture helpers, or `projectionIDFor*`
  imports.

Phase 1 is a hard architecture gate:

- `contract/projection/**` must exist before any cutover is called complete.
- Node DTOs, Swift DTOs, fixtures, and proof schemas must be generated from or
  checked against that package.
- `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` can remain only as migration
  history or be moved into the projection package. It cannot remain a second
  production display schema.

Swift render adapters have one final rule:

- A Swift type named `ThreadEvent` may exist only as a projection-row render
  adapter keyed by relay `projectionID`.
- Production Thread Detail, Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, and Host Registry
  render state must reject missing `displayOrderKey` instead of falling back to
  local date/turn/item/event sorting.
- Fallback sorting is allowed only in quarantined legacy tests that prove the
  old path has been retired; it is not allowed in production display stores or
  acceptance proof.

Enforcement is part of the architecture:

- Forbidden-pattern gates are not lint polish. They are the mechanism that
  keeps the architecture from drifting back into multiple identity owners.
- No implementation can be accepted while production display code or acceptance
  proof still contains raw display routes, fixture-computed expected IDs,
  permissive proof schemas, `logicalHostID::threadID` identity, `baseSeq`,
  `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`, `visibleEventIDs`, or request-card display
  IDs derived from `requestID`.

## Architecture Decision

The permanent answer is not "fix one duplicate." The permanent answer is a
single product projection plane:

```text
raw Codex adapters -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection store -> view streams -> Swift renderers
```

Only the relay projection engine answers these questions:

- What visible thing is this?
- What is its stable identity?
- What source fact produced it?
- What order should it render in?
- Is it fresh, stale, partial, or diagnostic?

Every production screen then consumes projection rows. Dock, Archive, Thread
Detail, request cards, simulator proof, and UI dump comparison all use the same
projection grammar. Raw `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
`thread/resume`, live notifications, and server requests become private input
adapters. They are not display contracts.

This is intentionally zero-sunk-cost. If an existing route, DTO, SQLite table,
test fixture, or proof script lets another layer infer visible identity, it is
not preserved for convenience. It is deleted, quarantined as a non-production
diagnostic, or rewritten to consume projection rows.

## Acceptance Standard

The architecture is accepted only when all of these are true:

- One schema source defines the shared projection envelope and typed view
  payloads.
- Node and Swift consume generated or schema-checked DTOs from that source.
- The relay has one pure projection engine for identity, source refs, order,
  freshness, and ledger operations.
- Dock and Archive cards are projection rows, not a separate `logicalHostID` /
  `host::thread` card grammar.
- Thread Detail messages and request cards are projection rows, not raw Codex
  rows normalized in Swift.
- Relay SQLite stores materialized projections keyed by projection contract
  version, source host, view membership, and projection identity.
- A projection contract version bump invalidates old materialized rows before
  they can be served as fresh.
- Swift display stores apply only projection snapshots and updates by
  `epoch`, `seq`, `projectionID`, and `displayOrderKey`.
- Swift never creates production visible IDs from raw Codex JSON, body text,
  timestamps, local UUIDs, WebSocket request IDs alone, or UI object lifetime.
- Proof scripts compare simulator accessibility state against relay projection
  snapshots or updates, not against a second reconstruction of raw Codex truth.
  Fields such as `expectedMessageEventIDs` are forbidden in acceptance proof
  outputs because they encode a second identity oracle.
- Test fixtures either come from the projection engine or validate against the
  projection schema. They do not invent production message/card IDs, and they
  do not compute expected UI IDs outside the relay-emitted projection ledger.
- Raw routes may exist only as relay-internal adapters, mutation routes, or
  named diagnostics. They cannot feed production display state or acceptance
  proof.

Net: after implementation, identity drift is not a category of app bug because
there is no second production identity owner left.

## Zero-Sunk-Cost Permanent Solution

The objectively clean architecture is a projection system, not a Thread Detail
fix.

The relay owns a single projection contract package. Raw Codex facts enter that
package; versioned projection rows leave it. Every user-visible Dock object is
then just a row in a projection view.

The architecture has seven laws:

1. Raw Codex routes are adapters only.
   `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, live
   notifications, and server requests may feed the relay, but they never define
   phone display identity.
2. One pure projection engine owns identity.
   The only production helpers that can create `sourceRef`, `projectionID`,
   `displayOrderKey`, row role, freshness, `identityVersion`, or
   `projectionEngineVersion` live in the relay projection contract package.
3. One ledger model owns updates.
   Dock, Archive, Archive Cleanup, Host Registry, and Thread Detail all use the
   same `snapshot`, `upsert`, `delete`, `heartbeat`, and `resyncRequired`
   semantics with `epoch`, `seq`, `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`, and
   `viewParamsKey`.
4. Swift is a renderer and validator.
   Swift decodes generated or schema-checked projection DTOs, validates the
   envelope, rejects gaps/mismatches, renders by `projectionID`, and sorts by
   `displayOrderKey`. It does not reconstruct visible identity from raw JSON,
   body text, timestamps, request IDs, UUIDs, or object lifetime.
5. `requestID` is never display identity.
   JSON-RPC `requestID` routes a response. If a request is visible, the visible
   row is still keyed by relay `projectionID`; request state is payload/revision.
6. Cache validity is part of the identity contract.
   Materialized rows are keyed by
   `schemaVersion + identityVersion + projectionEngineVersion + sourceHostID +
   view + viewParamsKey + projectionID`. A version bump cannot serve old rows as
   fresh.
7. Proof reads the emitted projection stream.
   Simulator/UI proof, live-filter proof, controlled fixtures, and acceptance
   reports compare the app only to relay-emitted projection snapshots/updates or
   a byte-for-byte retained witness export. They do not call `projectionIDFor*`
   helpers or reconstruct expected visible IDs beside the system under test.

That is the elegance test. There can be many raw inputs and many screens, but
there is one place where a visible object becomes a visible object. If a future
feature cannot go through that place, the feature is architecturally incomplete.

This deliberately rejects the cheaper alternatives:

- no Swift-side duplicate suppression;
- no body-text dedupe;
- no "prefer newest route" heuristic;
- no second identity helper in tests;
- no keeping raw routes as hidden display proof paths;
- no accepting stale cache rows because they are "compatible enough."

The end state is simple: the iPhone renders a projection view, and every row on
screen has exactly one relay projection identity.

## User-Visible Bug

When an outbound user message is sent, Thread Detail can show that outbound
message twice.

The intended behavior is simpler:

- One user send produces one visible user-message row.
- That row may move or lose its live badge as canonical history catches up.
- It must not remain as both a live row and a canonical row.

## Root Cause

The original pre-projection Thread Detail path had no single canonical event
identity layer for "the same Codex item" across live notifications and
canonical history reads.

That client path stored `ThreadEvent` rows in `ThreadEventIndex` and merged
only by:

1. Exact `ThreadEvent.id`.
2. A secondary stream key of `turnID + itemID + kind + visibility`.

That works only when every producer gives the same `turnID` and `itemID` in the
same place. The outbound path does not guarantee that.

The dangerous path is:

1. Thread Detail is live through `thread/resume`.
2. A user sends or otherwise creates a user message.
3. The live session can emit an `item/started` or `item/completed` notification.
4. The app turns that live notification into a `ThreadEvent`.
5. The Dock row updates, so Thread Detail does a canonical reread:
   `thread/read` + all pages of `thread/turns/list` + `thread/resume`.
6. That canonical reread is merged into the existing event index, not used as a
   replacement.
7. If the live row and canonical row do not normalize to the same event identity,
   both survive and render as two visible user-message cards.

That was a client-side merge contract bug. The current work-in-progress moves
the direct Thread Detail display path toward relay projection DTOs, but the
broader architecture is not complete until all display surfaces and proof paths
share the same projection identity plane.

## What This Is Not

This does not look like a SwiftUI `ForEach` rendering duplicate. `ForEach` keys
rows by `ThreadEventRenderRow.id`, which is `event.id`.

This does not look like an optimistic-send duplicate. `ThreadDetailStore.sendDraft`
does not add a local pending message row. It sends `turn/start` or `turn/steer`,
then clears the draft and updates `activeTurnID`.

This does not look like a relay "sent the same command twice" bug from the code
path alone. The relay forwards `turn/start` and `turn/steer` to the active
upstream after checking that the downstream detail session is bound to the same
thread. It does not create Thread Detail rows.

The duplicate is produced after the client accepts multiple representations of
the same logical Codex item and fails to collapse them.

## Permanent Architecture Proposal

The earlier narrow answer was "put Thread Detail row identity in the relay."
That is directionally right, but it is not the full permanent answer if the bar
is "this whole class of identity issues stops being a concern."

The full answer is one relay-owned projection identity plane for every
user-visible Dock object:

```text
raw Codex state -> relay projection engine -> versioned projection ledger -> Swift renderer
```

Swift, UI proof scripts, simulator fixtures, and tests should never separately
decide what a visible production row/card "is." They can render, validate, and
compare projection rows, but they do not own production identity.

This is a stronger architecture than a Thread Detail-only patch because the
same failure shape has already appeared in several forms:

- Dock cards were ordered from stale thread-level metadata while newer turn
  state existed somewhere else.
- Thread Detail could merge live and canonical rows under different IDs.
- Request cards had their own card/request identity beside message rows.
- Proof scripts reconstructed expected UI IDs instead of reading the relay's
  display ledger.
- Tests used fake/static snapshots that did not exercise real temporal
  convergence.

The permanent fix is therefore not "normalize one more payload field." The
permanent fix is to make visible identity, visible order, freshness, and update
continuity a single projection contract at the relay boundary.

### The Object Model

Use three separate concepts everywhere. Mixing them is what creates duplicates:

| Concept | Owner | Meaning | May change? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceRef` | Relay normalizer | Stable reference to the raw Codex fact, including host/thread/turn/item/request identity. | No, unless the relay emits a supersession from pending to canonical. |
| `projectionID` | Relay normalizer | Stable visible row/card identity derived from `sourceRef` plus row role. | No. |
| `revision` | Relay ledger | Version of the content for the same `projectionID`. | Yes. |

The renderer keys UI rows by `projectionID`. Content changes, streaming text,
request status changes, and canonical catch-up updates bump `revision`; they do
not create new row identity.

The canonical identity namespace should include host identity, not just
`threadID`, so two relays or two Codex homes cannot collide:

```text
host:<sourceHostID>/row:host
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/turn:<turnID>/item:<itemID>/row:<rowRole>
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/request:<requestID>/row:request
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/system:<systemKind>/<stableSourceSequence>
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/diagnostic:<stableHash>/row:unknown
```

Dock and Archive use the same thread-card identity:

```text
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
```

The route `view` decides whether that row appears in Dock or Archive. Archive
state is payload state, not a separate card identity. The Dock/Archive card
`sourceRef` is:

```text
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>
```

The existing Dock `logicalHostID` field is a transition alias for
`sourceHostID`; if a payload
carries both and they disagree, the relay must diagnose or resync instead of
letting Swift choose.

`sourceHostID` is the relay's canonical identity for the Codex source host. It
must be stable across Bonjour name changes, LAN/Tailscale endpoint changes, and
phone saved host config edits. UI labels can change; source identity cannot.

The derivation rule is:

1. Use non-empty `CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID` from relay-side configuration.
2. Else use the persisted value in `.codex-dock/source-host-id`.
3. Else create `.codex-dock/source-host-id` once as
   `local-<sha256(platform + user + CODEX_HOME + historyUrl)[0..12]>`.

`sourceHostID` must match `[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}`. It must not be
derived from endpoint hostnames, Bonjour names, LAN IPs, Tailscale names, saved
phone host config, WebSocket connection IDs, relay process IDs, or
`CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_INSTANCE_ID`.

### Projection Row Envelope

Every user-visible projection row should share one envelope, even when the row
payload is typed differently for Dock cards, Archive cards, Thread Detail
messages, and request cards:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "identityVersion": 1,
  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
  "view": "thread.detail",
  "threadID": "019e...",
  "projectionID": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1/row:userMessage",
  "sourceRef": "host:amir-m5/thread:019e.../turn:t1/item:i1",
  "rowRole": "userMessage",
  "revision": 7,
  "displayOrderKey": "9998239345599999|0000000000|9999999999|9999999999|...",
  "freshness": {
    "state": "fresh",
    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
  },
  "payload": {}
}
```

The row-specific payload can stay typed:

- Dock and Archive rows carry card fields.
- Thread Detail rows carry message/request/system fields.
- Request-backed rows carry `requestID` for responses, but the visible row key
  remains `projectionID`.

The shared envelope is what kills identity drift. The screen can vary; the
identity and update rules do not.

### Projection Snapshot And Update Envelope

Each subscribed view should use the same stream grammar:

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "identityVersion": 1,
  "view": "thread.detail",
  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
  "threadID": "019e...",
  "epoch": "projection-...",
  "seq": 42,
  "scope": "thread",
  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
  "complete": true,
  "freshness": {
    "state": "fresh",
    "asOf": "2026-06-01T18:00:00.000Z",
    "sourceWatermark": "codex-source-..."
  },
  "rows": []
}
```

Updates are only:

- `snapshot`: replace the declared scope.
- `upsert`: insert or replace rows by `projectionID`.
- `delete`: remove rows by `projectionID`.
- `heartbeat`: prove continuity without changing rows.
- `resyncRequired`: declare continuity broken and force a replacement
  snapshot.

Every update carries `epoch` and `seq`. Swift applies only the active epoch and
monotonic sequence. A new epoch without a snapshot is invalid. A sequence gap is
not "probably fine"; it is stale until resync succeeds.

Every projection snapshot and update also carries `projectionEngineVersion`.
Clients store the active engine version with the active epoch. If an update
arrives with a different `projectionEngineVersion` inside the same epoch, the
client rejects it and requests the matching resync route. A new engine version
is accepted only through a replacement snapshot with a new epoch.

`projectionEngineVersion` is required on every projection snapshot and update
envelope for Dock, Archive, Host Registry, and Thread Detail. Stored projection
rows also carry the engine version as cache metadata. If Swift sees an engine
version mismatch, it must not translate old rows locally; it marks the view
stale and asks the relay for a replacement snapshot.

The existing route names can remain because they are understandable:

- `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`
- `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, `archive/resync`
- `thread/detail/read`, `thread/detail/subscribe`, `thread/detail/update`,
  `thread/detail/resync`

The elegant part is not a single generic route name. The elegant part is that
all three route families obey the same projection envelope and identity rules.

### Cross-View Scope And Snapshot Authority

Thread Detail already names `scope: "thread"` and optional `scope: "window"`.
Dock and Archive need the same explicit authority rule so card cutover does not
recreate merge ambiguity under new names.

Accepted projection scopes:

| View | Scope | Meaning | Snapshot replacement rule |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `dock` | `view` | Complete active Dock view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `dock` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
| `archive` | `view` | Complete Archive view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local `archive` row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
| `archive.cleanup` | `view` | Complete Archive Cleanup candidate view for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local cleanup candidate row for that `sourceHostID` and `viewParamsKey` with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
| `dock` | `host` | Complete active Dock view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
| `archive` | `host` | Complete Archive view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
| `archive.cleanup` | `host` | Complete cleanup candidate view for one `sourceHostID`. | Replace only cleanup rows for that `sourceHostID`, `view`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
| `dock` / `archive` / `archive.cleanup` | `window` | Bounded key range inside a card-like view. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |
| `host.registry` | `view` | Complete host registry for the supplied `viewParamsKey`. | Replace every local host row for that registry view with the snapshot rows. Rows absent from the snapshot are deleted. |
| `thread.detail` | `thread` | Complete detail view for one thread. | Replace every local row for that `sourceHostID`, `threadID`, and `viewParamsKey`. |
| `thread.detail` | `window` | Bounded key range inside one thread. | Replace only rows whose `displayOrderKey` falls inside the declared window bounds. Missing bounds make the snapshot invalid. |

Dock and Archive stream envelopes omit `threadID` at the snapshot/update
envelope level unless the update is explicitly scoped to one thread. Card rows
carry `payload.threadID` and, when useful for validation, an envelope
`threadID`. Swift must not infer a Dock/Archive snapshot's authority from the
presence or absence of row IDs; it uses `view`, `scope`, `sourceHostID`,
`viewParamsKey`, and window bounds.

For every view:

- `snapshot` with `scope: "view"` or `scope: "host"` is authoritative for its
  declared scope.
- `snapshot` with `scope: "window"` is authoritative only for the declared
  order-key range.
- `upsert` inserts or replaces exact `projectionID`s.
- `delete` removes exact `projectionID`s.
- `heartbeat` proves continuity only; it never changes membership.
- `resyncRequired` makes the active view stale until the matching resync route
  returns a replacement snapshot.

### Dock And Archive Projection DTOs

Dock and Archive use the same required-field rigor as Thread Detail. The only
difference is the typed card payload and default scope.

`DockSnapshotDTO` and `ArchiveSnapshotDTO`:

```json
{
  "kind": "snapshot",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "identityVersion": 1,
  "projectionEngineVersion": 1,
  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
  "view": "dock",
  "epoch": "projection-...",
  "seq": 1,
  "scope": "view",
  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
  "complete": true,
  "order": "displayOrderKeyAscending",
  "freshness": {
    "state": "fresh"
  },
  "rows": []
}
```

`DockUpdateDTO` and `ArchiveUpdateDTO`:

```json
{
  "kind": "upsert",
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "identityVersion": 1,
  "projectionEngineVersion": 1,
  "sourceHostID": "amir-m5",
  "view": "dock",
  "epoch": "projection-...",
  "seq": 2,
  "scope": "view",
  "viewParamsKey": "sha256:...",
  "order": "displayOrderKeyAscending",
  "rows": [],
  "projectionIDs": []
}
```

Required fields by update kind are the same as Thread Detail, with `threadID`
omitted unless the card update is explicitly scoped to one thread. `delete`
uses `projectionIDs`; card streams do not have `deleteCardIDs`. `upsert` uses
`rows`; card streams do not have `upsertCards`.

Thread-card row payload:

```json
{
  "threadID": "019e...",
  "backendSessionID": "019e...",
  "title": "Hill climb experiment",
  "displaySummary": "Current work summary",
  "status": "running",
  "sourceKind": "human",
  "lane": "human",
  "archiveState": "active",
  "repository": "codex-client",
  "workingDirectory": "/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client",
  "branch": "main",
  "activityAt": "2026-06-01T19:50:00.000Z",
  "activityAtMs": 1780343400000,
  "relationship": "root",
  "forkedFromID": null,
  "hostDisplayName": "Amir M5",
  "hostEndpoint": "amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510"
}
```

`rowRole` for Dock/Archive cards is `threadCard`. The card `projectionID` is:

```text
host:<sourceHostID>/thread:<threadID>/row:threadCard
```

Dock and Archive thread-card `displayOrderKey` is:

```text
<invertedActivityMillis>|<statusPriority>|<safeProjectionID>
```

Field rules:

- `activityMillis` is the relay-proven newest activity time for the thread.
- `invertedActivityMillis = 9999999999999999 - activityMillis`, left-padded to
  16 decimal digits.
- `statusPriority` is left-padded to 4 decimal digits and is relay-owned:
  needs-approval/user-input before running before idle before error before
  unknown/dormant when activity ties exactly.
- `safeProjectionID` is the canonical escaped `projectionID` tie breaker.
- Swift compares the full string only; it never parses it back into fields.

Normative `statusPriority` values:

| Card status | Priority |
| --- | --- |
| `needsInput` | `0000` |
| `needsApproval` | `0000` |
| `running` | `0001` |
| `idle` | `0002` |
| `error` | `0003` |
| `unknown` | `0004` |
| any unrecognized active status | `0004` |
| `dormant` / not loaded | `0005` |

Archive Cleanup is its own relay-projected view:

```text

```

Routes:

- `archive/cleanup/subscribe`
- `archive/cleanup/update`
- `archive/cleanup/resync`


