51	public struct DockHostIdentityResolver: Equatable, Sendable {
52	    private struct HostRecord: Equatable, Sendable {
53	        var host: DockHostConfiguration
54	        var aliases: Set<String>
55	        var displayNames: [String]
56	        var endpoints: [String]
57	        var hasObservedLogicalIdentity: Bool
58	    }
59	
60	    private struct LogicalRecord: Equatable, Sendable {
61	        var logicalHostID: String
62	        var records: [HostRecord]
63	        var hasObservedLogicalIdentity: Bool
64	    }
65	
66	    public static let empty = DockHostIdentityResolver(hosts: [])
67	
68	    private let logicalRecordsByID: [String: LogicalRecord]
69	    private let logicalIDsByAlias: [String: Set<String>]
70	    private let logicalIDByConfiguredHostID: [String: String]
71	    private let hostStatuses: [String: DockHostLoadStatus]
72	
73	    public init(
74	        hosts: [DockHostConfiguration],
75	        observations: [DockHostIdentityObservation] = [],
76	        hostStatuses: [String: DockHostLoadStatus] = [:]
77	    ) {
78	        let observationsByConfiguredHostID = Dictionary(grouping: observations, by: \.configuredHostID)
79	        self.hostStatuses = hostStatuses
80	
81	        var logicalRecordsByID: [String: LogicalRecord] = [:]
82	        var logicalIDByConfiguredHostID: [String: String] = [:]
83	
84	        for host in hosts {
85	            let hostObservations = observationsByConfiguredHostID[host.id] ?? []
86	            let observedLogicalHostID = Self.firstNonEmpty(
87	                hostObservations.map(\.logicalHostID) + hostObservations.map(\.streamHostID)
88	            )
89	            let logicalHostID = observedLogicalHostID ?? host.id
90	            logicalIDByConfiguredHostID[host.id] = logicalHostID
91	
92	            var aliases = Set<String>()
93	            [
94	                host.id,
95	                host.displayName,
96	                host.endpoint.displayEndpoint,
97	                logicalHostID
98	            ].forEach { Self.insertAlias($0, into: &aliases) }
99	            for observation in hostObservations {
100	                [
101	                    observation.configuredHostID,
102	                    observation.streamHostID,
103	                    observation.logicalHostID,
104	                    observation.displayName,
105	                    observation.endpoint
106	                ].forEach { Self.insertAlias($0, into: &aliases) }
107	            }
108	
109	            let displayNames = Self.uniqueNonEmpty(
110	                hostObservations.map(\.displayName) + [host.displayName, logicalHostID]
111	            )
112	            let endpoints = Self.uniqueNonEmpty(
113	                hostObservations.map(\.endpoint) + [host.endpoint.displayEndpoint]
114	            )
115	            let record = HostRecord(
116	                host: host,
117	                aliases: aliases,
118	                displayNames: displayNames,
119	                endpoints: endpoints,
120	                hasObservedLogicalIdentity: observedLogicalHostID != nil
121	            )
122	
123	            var logicalRecord = logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID]
124	                ?? LogicalRecord(
125	                    logicalHostID: logicalHostID,
126	                    records: [],
127	                    hasObservedLogicalIdentity: false
128	                )
129	            logicalRecord.records.append(record)
130	            logicalRecord.hasObservedLogicalIdentity = logicalRecord.hasObservedLogicalIdentity || record.hasObservedLogicalIdentity
131	            logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID] = logicalRecord
132	        }
133	
134	        var logicalIDsByAlias: [String: Set<String>] = [:]
135	        for logicalRecord in logicalRecordsByID.values {
136	            for record in logicalRecord.records {
137	                for alias in record.aliases {
138	                    logicalIDsByAlias[alias, default: []].insert(logicalRecord.logicalHostID)
139	                    logicalIDsByAlias[Self.normalizedAlias(alias), default: []].insert(logicalRecord.logicalHostID)
140	                }
141	            }
142	        }
143	
144	        self.logicalRecordsByID = logicalRecordsByID
145	        self.logicalIDByConfiguredHostID = logicalIDByConfiguredHostID
146	        self.logicalIDsByAlias = logicalIDsByAlias
147	    }
148	
149	    public func logicalHostID(
150	        forAlias alias: String,
151	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
152	    ) -> String? {
153	        let aliasLogicalIDs = logicalIDs(forAlias: alias)
154	        if let sourceConfiguredHostID,
155	           let sourceLogicalID = logicalIDByConfiguredHostID[sourceConfiguredHostID],
156	           aliasLogicalIDs.isEmpty || aliasLogicalIDs.contains(sourceLogicalID) {
157	            return sourceLogicalID
158	        }
159	        guard aliasLogicalIDs.count == 1 else {
160	            return nil
161	        }
162	        return aliasLogicalIDs.first
163	    }
164	
165	    public func migrationLogicalHostID(
166	        forAlias alias: String,
167	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
168	    ) -> String? {
169	        guard let logicalHostID = logicalHostID(
170	            forAlias: alias,
171	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
172	        ),
173	              let logicalRecord = logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID],
174	              logicalRecord.hasObservedLogicalIdentity else {
175	            return nil
176	        }
177	        return logicalHostID
178	    }
179	
180	    public func resolve(
181	        rowHostID: String,
182	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil,
183	        preferredConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
184	    ) -> ResolvedDockHost? {
185	        let logicalHostID = logicalHostID(
186	            forAlias: rowHostID,
187	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
188	        )
189	        guard let logicalHostID,
190	              let logicalRecord = logicalRecordsByID[logicalHostID] else {
191	            return nil
192	        }
193	
194	        guard let selectedRecord = preferredRecord(
195	            in: logicalRecord,
196	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID,
197	            preferredConfiguredHostID: preferredConfiguredHostID
198	        ) else {
199	            return nil
200	        }
201	
202	        return ResolvedDockHost(
203	            logicalHostID: logicalHostID,
204	            host: selectedRecord.host,
205	            configuredHostIDs: logicalRecord.records.map(\.host.id),
206	            displayName: selectedRecord.displayNames.first ?? selectedRecord.host.displayName,
207	            endpoint: selectedRecord.endpoints.first ?? selectedRecord.host.endpoint.displayEndpoint
208	        )
209	    }
210	
211	    public func contains(
212	        rowHostID: String,
213	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil,
214	        in configuredHostID: String
215	    ) -> Bool {
216	        guard let expectedLogicalID = logicalIDByConfiguredHostID[configuredHostID] else {
217	            return false
218	        }
219	        let rowLogicalIDs = logicalIDs(forAlias: rowHostID)
220	        guard rowLogicalIDs.count == 1,
221	              rowLogicalIDs.contains(expectedLogicalID) else {
222	            return false
223	        }
224	        guard let sourceConfiguredHostID else {
225	            return true
226	        }
227	        let sourceLogicalIDs = logicalIDs(forAlias: sourceConfiguredHostID)
228	        if sourceLogicalIDs.isEmpty,
229	           sourceConfiguredHostID == configuredHostID {
230	            return true
231	        }
232	        return sourceLogicalIDs.count == 1 && sourceLogicalIDs.contains(expectedLogicalID)
233	    }
234	
235	    public func displayName(
236	        forAlias alias: String,
237	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
238	    ) -> String? {
239	        resolve(
240	            rowHostID: alias,
241	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
242	        )?.displayName
243	    }
244	
245	    public func endpoint(
246	        forAlias alias: String,
247	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil
248	    ) -> String? {
249	        resolve(
250	            rowHostID: alias,
251	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
252	        )?.endpoint
253	    }
254	
255	    public func state(
256	        forAlias alias: String,
257	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String? = nil,
258	        in states: [DockHostStateViewModel]
259	    ) -> DockHostStateViewModel? {
260	        guard let resolved = resolve(
261	            rowHostID: alias,
262	            sourceConfiguredHostID: sourceConfiguredHostID
263	        ) else {
264	            return nil
265	        }
266	        return states.first { resolved.configuredHostIDs.contains($0.host.id) }
267	    }
268	
269	    private func logicalIDs(forAlias alias: String) -> Set<String> {
270	        let trimmed = alias.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
271	        guard !trimmed.isEmpty else {
272	            return []
273	        }
274	        return logicalIDsByAlias[trimmed]
275	            ?? logicalIDsByAlias[Self.normalizedAlias(trimmed)]
276	            ?? []
277	    }
278	
279	    private func preferredRecord(
280	        in logicalRecord: LogicalRecord,
281	        sourceConfiguredHostID: String?,
282	        preferredConfiguredHostID: String?
283	    ) -> HostRecord? {
284	        if let sourceConfiguredHostID,
285	           let record = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { $0.host.id == sourceConfiguredHostID }) {
286	            return record
287	        }
288	        if let preferredConfiguredHostID,
289	           let record = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { $0.host.id == preferredConfiguredHostID }) {
290	            return record
291	        }
292	        if let loadedRecord = logicalRecord.records.first(where: { isLoadedStatus(hostStatuses[$0.host.id]) }) {
293	            return loadedRecord
294	        }
295	        return logicalRecord.records.first
296	    }
297	
298	    private func isLoadedStatus(_ status: DockHostLoadStatus?) -> Bool {
299	        guard let status else {
300	            return false
301	        }
302	        switch status {
303	        case .loaded, .degraded, .empty:
304	            return true
305	        case .checking, .offline, .error:
306	            return false
307	        }
308	    }
309	
310	    private static func insertAlias(_ value: String?, into aliases: inout Set<String>) {
311	        guard let value = nonEmpty(value) else {
312	            return
313	        }
314	        aliases.insert(value)
315	    }
316	
317	    private static func uniqueNonEmpty(_ values: [String?]) -> [String] {
318	        var seen: Set<String> = []
319	        var result: [String] = []
320	        for value in values {
321	            guard let value = nonEmpty(value),
322	                  seen.insert(value).inserted else {
323	                continue
324	            }
325	            result.append(value)
326	        }
327	        return result
328	    }
329	
330	    private static func firstNonEmpty(_ values: [String?]) -> String? {
331	        values.lazy.compactMap(nonEmpty).first
332	    }
333	
334	    private static func nonEmpty(_ value: String?) -> String? {
335	        let trimmed = value?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
336	        guard let trimmed, !trimmed.isEmpty else {
337	            return nil
338	        }
339	        return trimmed
340	    }
341	
342	    private static func normalizedAlias(_ value: String) -> String {
343	        value.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).lowercased()
344	    }
345	}

15	# Pinned Unpin Menu And Degraded Health
16	
17	## TL;DR
18	
19	<!-- bugs:block:tldr -->
20	
21	Symptom: On Amir's physical iPhone 17 Pro after app startup, five pinned rows were visible. Two could be unpinned, then the remaining three were stuck. Swiping a pinned row no longer reliably exposed the `Unpin` action; sometimes the action appeared briefly and disappeared before it could be tapped. The same clean rebuild also showed partially connected health: Dock feed degraded, thread detail degraded, archive degraded, voice degraded, and diagnostics degraded.
22	
23	Impact: Pinned rows can become effectively impossible to unpin from the primary Dock UI, and the system health UI can report broad degradation even after relays were restarted, making it unclear whether the client is live, stale, or only partially connected.
24	
25	Most likely cause: two separate client-side problems. First, the pinned section is a custom `UICollectionView` bridge that calls `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update; live Dock updates or height/layout updates during a swipe can close UIKit swipe actions, matching the "menu pops in and out" symptom. Second, the health UI is treating a capped Dock row window (`Home: Showing 250 of 964`) as global service degradation, then applying that same fallback to Dock feed, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics when no route evidence has been loaded.
26	
27	Next action: review the cross-linked architecture plan before implementing. Do not patch production code yet. The physical iPhone 17 Pro is explicitly out of scope for remote commands.
28	
29	Status: root cause found; fix not implemented.
30	
31	<!-- /bugs:block:tldr -->
32	
33	## Bug North Star
34	
35	The app should let a user unpin any visible pinned Dock row with a stable, tappable action. Live stream updates, route-health refreshes, layout recalculation, worker activity, or startup recovery should not make the swipe action disappear before the user can tap it.
36	
37	The health UI should distinguish "relay process is reachable but route proof is not yet available" from true degradation. A clean rebuild against restarted healthy relays should not show every major feature as degraded unless there is concrete route-level failure evidence.
38	
39	Architecture plan: [pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-architecture-plan-2026-06-02.md](./pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-architecture-plan-2026-06-02.md).
40	
41	## Scope And Constraints
42	
43	- Do not query, install to, launch on, log from, or otherwise control the physical iPhone 17 Pro during this investigation.
44	- Use source code, local relay diagnostics, logs, and the `iPhone 17` simulator for reproduction.
45	- Analyze first. Do not modify production code until the bug is fix-ready and Amir asks for the fix.
46	- Keep this document as the source of truth for evidence and decisions.
47	
48	## Evidence
49	
50	<!-- bugs:block:analysis -->
51	
52	### User-Reported Evidence
53	
54	- Physical iPhone 17 Pro cannot be remotely controlled for this diagnosis.
55	- After startup, five pinned rows were visible.
56	- Two pinned rows could be unpinned successfully.
57	- Three pinned rows remained stuck.
58	- Swiping a stuck pinned row does not reliably show the `Unpin` menu.
59	- Sometimes the `Unpin` menu appears and disappears before it can be tapped.
60	- Same app state reports partially connected health:
61	  - Dock feed degraded
62	  - Thread detail degraded
63	  - Archive degraded
64	  - Voice degraded
65	  - Diagnostics degraded
66	- This happened after a clean rebuild and relay restarts.
67	
68	### Current Repo/Runtime Baseline
69	
70	- Time captured: `2026-06-02T12:03:10Z`.
71	- Repo: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`.
72	- Branch commit at the time of investigation start was previously deployed as `e048b5d Unify Dock projection identity`.
73	- The first diagnostic pass used source reads only and avoided all physical-device commands after Amir unplugged the iPhone 17 Pro.
74	
75	### Runtime Evidence: Relay Health Was Not The Broad Failure
76	
77	Relay route summaries were collected from both configured hosts:
78	
79	- `http://amir-m5.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
80	- `http://home.fairy-salmon.ts.net:4510`
81	
82	Both relays returned `/syncz` as:
83	
84	```json
85	{"ok":true,"service":"codex-dock-relay","schema":"codexdock.syncz.v1","state":"available"}
86	```
87	
88	The route summaries did not show app-critical failures. They showed a mix of healthy exercised routes and unknown passive/manual routes:
89	
90	- `dock/resync`, `dock/subscribe`, and `initialize` had healthy evidence on at least the local host path.
91	- `dock/update`, `thread/detail/*`, archive mutation/update routes, and voice routes were mostly `unknown` because they are passive/manual routes and had not been exercised.
92	- `appCriticalFailures` was `[]` on both hosts.
93	
94	Inference: the relays were reachable. Unknown route evidence exists, but that is not the same as a failed relay. The user-visible "everything degraded" screen needed client-side explanation.
95	
96	### Simulator Evidence: Health Degradation Is A Dock Window Fallback
97	
98	The `iPhone 17` simulator was launched with:
99	
100	```bash
101	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
102	```
103	
104	Accessibility dump evidence from the Dock screen:
105	
106	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
107	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=0; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; 487 shown ... Partial`
108	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` label:
109	  - `Online 2/2`
110	- `codexdock.connectivity.global` value:
111	  - `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`
112	
113	After opening System Health from the global indicator, accessibility showed:
114	
115	- Summary:
116	  - `Partial`
117	  - `Home: Showing 250 of 964`
118	- `codexdock.system-health.category.dockFeed`:
119	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
120	- `codexdock.system-health.category.threadDetail`:
121	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
122	- `codexdock.system-health.category.archive`:
123	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
124	- `codexdock.system-health.category.voice`:
125	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
126	- `codexdock.system-health.category.diagnostics`:
127	  - `Degraded. Home: Showing 250 of 964 Run check or open host details.`
128	
129	Opening the `Home` host detail showed:
130	
131	- `State, Showing 250 of 964`
132	- `Technical Evidence`
133	- `No route evidence yet.`
134	
135	Conclusion: the System Health screen degraded every category without route-level evidence. It copied the global Dock row-window partial message into unrelated feature categories.
136	
137	### Code Anchor: Dock Row Windows Become Connectivity Partial
138	
139	The row-window state originates in `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`.
140	
141	Relevant source anchors:
142	
143	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:428-435`: if a stream snapshot is not complete, `hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: visibleRows, message: "Showing \(visibleRows) of \(knownTotal)")`.
144	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:364`: `DockRenderInput.isPartial` becomes true if any host is checking or partial.
145	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:278-296`: loaded Dock snapshots are reported to `AppConnectivityStore`.
146	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:419-437`: `.partial(_, message)` Dock host status becomes `HostConnectivityPhase.partial(message)`.
147	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift:610-616`: if all hosts are online-like but at least one is partial, the global status becomes `.partial("\(host): \(message)")`.
148	
149	This means `Home: Showing 250 of 964` is currently treated as global connectivity partiality even though it is actually a data-window completeness fact.
150	
151	### Code Anchor: System Health Falls Back From Global Partial To Every Category
152	
153	Relevant source anchors:
154	
155	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:66-68`: System Health projects from `store.hosts` and `store.overallStatus`.
156	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift:50-57`: route diagnostics are only fetched by tapping `Run check`; they are not fetched on open.
157	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:31-35`: if a category has no route diagnostics, it uses `fallbackStatus(for:overallStatus:)`.
158	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift:78-79`: global `.partial(message)` maps to category `.degraded(message, nextAction: "Run check or open host details.")`.
159	
160	This is the exact code path that reproduced in the simulator: the `Home` row-window partial became a global `.partial`, then every category with no route evidence displayed `Degraded`.
161	
162	### Code Anchor: Pinned Rows Are A Custom UIKit Collection View
163	
164	Pinned rows do not use the normal SwiftUI `DockSwipeActionRow` path. In `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`, body rows use `dockRow(row, resetToken:)`, but pinned rows use `dockPinnedRow(row)` inside `DockPinnedSectionView`.
165	
166	Relevant source anchors:
167	
168	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:729`: renders `DockPinnedSectionView` when `projection.pinnedRows` is not empty.
169	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:733`: pinned reorder callback calls `Task { await store.reorderPinnedRows(rows) }`.
170	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:734`: pinned unpin callback calls `Task { await store.setPinned(false, for: row) }`.
171	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:859`: `dockPinnedRow(_:)` renders only `dockRowContent`, with `showsContextMenu: false`.
172	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:219`: pinned rows render through `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView`.
173	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:274`: `makeUIView` creates a `UICollectionView`.
174	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:279`: trailing swipe actions are provided by `UICollectionLayoutListConfiguration.trailingSwipeActionsConfigurationProvider`.
175	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:310`: `updateUIView` runs on SwiftUI updates.
176	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:315-320`: when not moving, `updateUIView` assigns `workingRows = rows`, calls `collectionView.reloadData()`, invalidates layout, forces layout, and reports measured height.
177	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:425-428`: the `Unpin` contextual action calls `parent.onUnpin(row)` and completes.
178	
179	First inference: any SwiftUI update to the pinned section while a UIKit trailing swipe action is open can cause `reloadData()`. UIKit list reloads close open swipe actions. This matches the user-visible symptom where the menu appears briefly and disappears.
180	
181	### Code Anchor: Body Rows Use A Separate Swipe Implementation
182	
183	Body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`, a SwiftUI view with local `offset` state.
184	
185	Relevant source anchors:
186	
187	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:8`: `DockSwipeActionRow`.
188	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:16`: local `@State private var offset`.
189	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:30`: `.simultaneousGesture(dragGesture)`.
190	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift:42-50`: row ID, pin state, and render revision changes close the action.
191	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift:832`: body rows use `DockSwipeActionRow`.
192	
193	First inference: pinned rows and body rows use materially different interaction implementations. A bug in pinned unpin can exist even if body row pin/unpin behaves normally.
194	
195	### Code Anchor: Pin/Unpin Is Local Metadata
196	
197	Relevant source anchors:
198	
199	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:208`: `setPinned(_:for:)`.
200	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:209-215`: pin/unpin persists through `persistMetadataChange`.
201	- `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift:93-100`: setting pinned updates `pinnedAt` and `pinnedOrder`; unpin clears both.
202	
203	First inference: the stuck swipe menu is likely an interaction/rendering issue before the `setPinned(false, for:)` action fires. The user's report says the menu often cannot be tapped; that is different from tapping `Unpin` and having persistence fail.
204	
205	### Simulator Evidence: Five Pinned Rows Survive Startup
206	
207	The simulator initially had no metadata file:
208	
209	- App container: `.../Library/Application Support/CodexDock`
210	- `thread-metadata.json`: absent
211	
212	To approximate the physical-phone startup state without touching the physical phone, five current `Amir-M5` Dock rows were seeded into the simulator's own app data as pinned local metadata. Each entry used the real app key shape:
213	
214	- `hostID`
215	- `backendSessionID`
216	- `threadID`
217	- `isPinned`
218	- `pinnedAt`
219	- `pinnedOrder`
220	
221	After relaunching with:
222	
223	```bash
224	FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'
225	```
226	
227	Accessibility showed:
228	
229	- `codexdock.dock.root` value:
230	  - `loaded; rows=487; pinned=5; lens=newest; search=false; filters=0; ... Partial`
231	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.toggle` value:
232	  - `Expanded, Pinned 5`
233	- `codexdock.dock.pinned.header` text:
234	  - `Pinned 5`
235	
236	Conclusion: persisted local pin metadata is loaded and projected correctly after startup in the simulator. The remaining bug is not "pins vanish on restart"; it is the pinned interaction surface becoming unstable after pins are present.
237	
238	### Simulator Evidence: Pinned Section Accessibility Shape Is Suspicious
239	
240	With five pins seeded, the accessibility tree showed:
241	
242	- Pinned header at `y=303`.
243	- Only one visible pinned row element was exposed at `y=782`.
244	- That row had value ending in `Pinned`.
245	
246	This does not by itself prove a layout bug, because accessibility listing only reports visible elements and the embedded collection is tall. But it reinforces that the pinned section is a large embedded UIKit surface with its own cell layout, not the same simple SwiftUI row stack used by body rows.
247	
248	### Testing Tool Drift: `sim-ui-dump` Contract Is Not Trustworthy Right Now
249	
250	Before seeded pins, `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` produced useful files but exited nonzero because the proof schema rejected the dump:
251	
252	```text
253	proof report contract check failed: /tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json/app: must NOT have additional properties
254	```
255	
256	This means the simulator dump producer and `contract/proof/sim-ui-dump.schema.json` have drifted. The dump still wrote:
257	
258	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.json`
259	- `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T120545Z/sim-ui-dump.md`
260	
261	After seeding five pinned rows, a second `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` hung during the current visible screen XCTest path and had to be killed. The lower-level Mobile MCP accessibility dump still worked and captured the pinned state. This is relevant because the formal proof path is currently weak around exactly the UI state under investigation.
262	
263	## Investigation Log
264	
265	### 2026-06-02T12:03Z Initial Source Triage
266	
267	Actions:
268	
269	- Confirmed active goal and physical iPhone 17 Pro no-touch constraint.
270	- Searched source for `pin`, `pinned`, `unpin`, `swipeActions`, `contextMenu`, degraded health, and route-health terms.
271	- Read `DockPinnedViews.swift`, `DockView.swift`, `DockStore.swift`, and `DockCardProjection.swift`.
272	
273	Learned:
274	
275	- Pinned rows are implemented as a custom UIKit `UICollectionView` list with trailing swipe actions and long-press reorder.
276	- Pinned rows call `reloadData()` on every SwiftUI update when not actively moving.
277	- Body rows use a separate SwiftUI offset-based swipe row and are not equivalent to pinned rows.
278	- Pinned row content intentionally disables the normal context menu.
279	- Unpin persistence is local metadata; the observed failure is probably before persistence because the action cannot be stably tapped.
280	
281	### 2026-06-02T12:07Z Relay And Health Evidence
282	
283	Actions:
284	
285	- Queried local and home relay health endpoints.
286	- Opened System Health in the `iPhone 17` simulator through accessibility, not screenshots.
287	- Opened `Home` host detail inside System Health.
288	- Read `ThreadCardTable`, `AppConnectivityStore`, `SystemHealthView`, and `SystemHealthProjector`.
289	
290	Learned:
291	
292	- Relays were reachable and `/syncz` returned `state=available`.
293	- The simulator global indicator showed `Online 2/2`, but value `Partial: Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
294	- System Health showed every category degraded for the same reason: `Home: Showing 250 of 964`.
295	- The `Home` host detail said `No route evidence yet.`
296	- Code confirms route diagnostics are not auto-fetched when System Health opens; the `Run check` button is the fetch path.
297	- Code confirms global `.partial` falls back to category `.degraded` when a category has no route evidence.
298	
299	Conclusion:
300	
301	The broad degraded UI is a client classification bug. A capped Dock row window is being presented as feature degradation across unrelated categories.
302	
303	### 2026-06-02T12:11Z Simulator Pinned-State Reproduction
304	
305	Actions:
306	
307	- Confirmed simulator app data had no existing `thread-metadata.json`.
308	- Fetched current Dock cards from the relay card stream to avoid guessing metadata keys.
309	- Seeded five simulator-only local metadata pins using real `hostID/backendSessionID/threadID` keys.
310	- Relaunched the app with `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'`.
311	- Dumped visible simulator accessibility via Mobile MCP against the simulator UDID.
312	
313	Learned:
314	
315	- The simulator Dock loaded with `pinned=5`.
316	- The pinned header displayed `Pinned 5`.
317	- At least one pinned row was visible and carried accessibility value `Pinned`.
318	- Pin persistence and projection survived restart.
319	
320	Conclusion:
321	
322	The remaining pinned problem is focused on the interaction layer: exposing and tapping `Unpin` on pinned rows.
323	
324	### 2026-06-02T12:13Z Formal UI Dump Gap
325	
326	Actions:
327	
328	- Ran `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` after seeded pins.
329	- Stopped the dump after it hung.
330	
331	Learned:
332	
333	- The first dump before seeded pins already revealed schema drift: top-level `app` exists in produced JSON but is rejected by the proof schema.
334	- The second dump hung in `CodexDockCurrentUIDumpTests/testDumpsCurrentVisibleScreenOnce`; only config was written under `/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-dump-20260602T121309Z/`.
335	- Mobile MCP accessibility dumping still worked.
336	
337	Conclusion:
338	
339	Our simulator proof path has blind spots in this class of bug. It can fail schema validation or hang in the precise pinned/high-text accessibility state we need to diagnose.
340	
341	## Ranked Hypotheses
342	
343	### H1: Pinned UIKit `reloadData()` closes swipe actions during live updates
344	
345	Confidence: high after source triage plus simulator pinned-state reproduction; not yet instrumented with a swipe-open timestamp.
346	
347	Mechanism:
348	
349	- User swipes a pinned row.
350	- UIKit opens the trailing `Unpin` action.
351	- A live Dock update, projection revision, health state update, height measurement callback, or other SwiftUI state change re-runs `updateUIView`.
352	- `updateUIView` calls `collectionView.reloadData()`.
353	- UIKit closes the open swipe action.
354	- User sees the menu pop in and out before it can be tapped.
355	
356	Why it fits:
357	
358	- The symptom is instability of the menu, not a failed `Unpin` action after tap.
359	- It can be worse after startup, when streams/health/status updates are still settling.
360	- It can be worse with live work happening, because updates keep arriving.
361	- It is specific to pinned rows because pinned rows use a collection view bridge.
362	
363	What would prove it:
364	
365	- Simulator reproduction where opening a pinned-row swipe action followed by a live Dock update or forced render update closes the action.
366	- Logs/instrumentation showing `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView.updateUIView`/`reloadData()` happens while the swipe action is open.
367	- A UI dump or XCTest proof showing `Unpin` action appears and disappears across samples without user tapping it.
368	
369	Current evidence:
370	
371	- The exact code path calls `collectionView.reloadData()` on every `updateUIView` while not moving.
372	- The simulator reproduced the same five-pinned startup state.
373	- The app is live and continuously receiving Dock stream/health changes.
374	- UIKit list reloads are known to close active cell swipe actions.
375	
376	This is the most direct explanation for the reported "appears then disappears" menu behavior.
377	
378	### H2: Long-press reorder recognizer competes with swipe recognizer
379	
380	Confidence: medium.
381	
382	Mechanism:
383	
384	- Pinned rows add a `UILongPressGestureRecognizer` for drag reorder with `minimumPressDuration = 0.35`.
385	- The recognizer has `cancelsTouchesInView = true`.
386	- Gesture delegate returns false for simultaneous recognition when either gesture is a long press.
387	- Slow/hesitant swipes could be interpreted as long press/reorder attempts, canceling the swipe action.
388	
389	Why it fits:
390	
391	- User describes inconsistent menu behavior.
392	- Pinned rows uniquely combine swipe actions and long-press reordering.
393	
394	What would prove it:
395	
396	- Simulator reproduction where slow swipes fail but fast swipes work.
397	- Gesture logs showing long-press began/canceled near failed swipe attempts.
398	
399	### H3: Hidden pinned rows by filter/scope are being mistaken for stuck pinned rows
400	
401	Confidence: low-medium.
402	
403	Mechanism:
404	
405	- `DockCardProjection` computes `pinnedRows` only from filtered rows.
406	- `allPinnedRows` includes all pinned rows.
407	- If filters/scope hide pinned rows, header can show `Pinned X of Y`.
408	
409	Why it partially fits:
410	
411	- User had five pinned, then two unpinned, leaving three.
412	- Existing UI has hidden pinned summary paths.
413	
414	Why it does not fit well:
415	
416	- User says the three rows are visible and swipe actions are unstable, not hidden.
417	- This does not explain the swipe menu appearing and disappearing.
418	
419	What would prove/disprove it:
420	
421	- UI dump showing header/title, visible pinned row count, active filters, and actual pinned summary.
422	
423	### H4: Unpin persistence fails after tap
424	
425	Confidence: low based on current report.
426	
427	Mechanism:
428	
429	- `metadataEngine.setPinned(false, for:)` throws.
430	- `persistMetadataChange` sets an action error and pinned state remains.
431	
432	Why it does not fit well:
433	
434	- User specifically reports not getting a stable unpin menu.
435	- Need evidence of a tap completing and a persistence error before elevating this.
436	
437	What would prove it:
438	
439	- `DockLog` action error or metadata write error after tapping `Unpin`.
440	
441	### H5: Health categories are degraded because route health is unproven/unknown after restart
442	
443	Confidence: superseded.
444	
445	This was the first health hypothesis, but the simulator proved a different specific path. Unknown route evidence is real, but unknown-only diagnostics are not what caused the observed broad degraded labels. The observed labels happened because no route evidence had been loaded into the System Health view, so it fell back from global `.partial`.
446	
447	### H6: Dock row-window partiality is incorrectly reused as broad service degradation
448	
449	Confidence: high; reproduced in simulator and confirmed in code.
450	
451	Mechanism:
452	
453	- Home relay has more rows than the current Dock stream window limit.
454	- `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)` returns `.partial(rowCount: 250, message: "Showing 250 of 964")`.
455	- `AppConnectivityStore.reportDockState` records that as `HostConnectivityPhase.partial("Showing 250 of 964")`.
456	- Overall connectivity becomes `.partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964")`.
457	- System Health opens without route diagnostics because `refreshRelayDiagnostics()` only runs from `Run check`.
458	- `SystemHealthProjector` sees no category route diagnostics and maps global `.partial` to `.degraded` for every category.
459	
460	Why it fits:
461	
462	- Simulator exactly displayed this state.
463	- Host detail exactly showed `No route evidence yet`.
464	- Every category used the same Dock window message.
465	- Relay `/syncz` was available and app-critical failures were empty.
466	
467	What would prove it further:
468	
469	- A unit test where `SystemHealthProjector.snapshot(hosts: [Home partial window], overallStatus: .partial("Home: Showing 250 of 964"))` with empty `routeDiagnostics` proves every category is currently degraded.
470	- A corrected test where row-window partiality no longer maps to service degradation.
471	
472	## Verification Plan
473	
474	1. Inspect health category mapping in Swift and route-health semantics in relay scripts.
475	2. Capture current local and home relay `/statusz`, `/routesz`, and `/syncz` payload summaries.
476	3. Run `rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` or `FORCE_LAUNCH=1 rtk make app SIM='iPhone 17'` as needed.
477	4. Use simulator UI dump before and after pinning/unpinning where possible:
478	   - `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'`
479	5. Create or use existing UI automation/accessibility path to pin several rows, restart/relaunch the simulator app, and sample pinned-row action visibility.
480	6. Capture simulator logs:
481	   - `rtk make sim-logs SIM='iPhone 17'`
482	7. Update this doc with proved root cause, disproved theories, and fix-ready status only when evidence is strong.
483	
484	## Fix Plan
485	
486	<!-- bugs:block:fix_plan -->
487	
488	Not implemented. Proposed shape for review:
489	
490	1. Split "Dock data window is partial" from "connectivity/service health is degraded."
491	   - `Showing 250 of 964` is a Dock data completeness/status message.
492	   - It should not drive global connectivity or System Health feature degradation by itself.
493	   - Keep the message visible in Dock where row-window completeness matters.
494	2. Make System Health route-evidence based.
495	   - Opening System Health should either fetch route diagnostics automatically or clearly show `Not checked` until the user runs a check.
496	   - A category should be `Degraded` only for direct failed/degraded/stale evidence in that category, not because Dock has a capped row window.
497	3. Replace the pinned row interaction path with one stable implementation.
498	   - Preferred permanent fix: stop using the custom embedded `UICollectionView` for pinned rows if reorder can be achieved with a SwiftUI-native list/stack path, or at least stop unconditional `reloadData()` during normal updates.
499	   - If keeping UIKit temporarily, update only changed rows with diffable data source or batch updates and never call `reloadData()` while a swipe action is open.
500	   - Reevaluate the long-press reorder recognizer so it does not cancel swipe actions.
501	4. Add tests for live-like behavior, not static snapshots only.
502	   - Pinned row UI test: seed or pin 5 rows, relaunch, open a pinned row swipe action, inject/replay a Dock update, assert `Unpin` remains visible long enough to tap.
503	   - Health projector test: capped Dock row window does not mark thread detail/archive/voice/diagnostics degraded.
504	   - System Health UI/accessibility test: with no route evidence, categories show `Not checked` or route-specific healthy/degraded states, not copied Dock window text.
505	   - Fix `sim-ui-dump` schema drift and add a regression so producer and schema cannot drift.
506	
507	<!-- /bugs:block:fix_plan -->
508	
509	## Implementation
510	
511	<!-- bugs:block:implementation -->
512	
513	No code changes made in analyze mode.
514	
515	<!-- /bugs:block:implementation -->

17	
18	# Architecture Plan: Pinned Unpin Stability And Honest Health State
19	
20	## TL;DR
21	
22	This is not a tiny tweak plan. The permanent fix is to remove the two duplicated meanings that caused this class of bugs:
23	
24	1. Pinned rows must not have a private UIKit interaction path. Normal rows and pinned rows should use one SwiftUI row-action owner.
25	2. A capped data window like `Showing 250 of 964` must not be represented as service or connectivity degradation.
26	
27	The model-consensus result is: enforce one owner per fact. Delete the pinned `UICollectionView` bridge from normal rendering, move reorder into a dedicated SwiftUI reorder surface, split the shared host load status so window completeness is not health, make System Health route-evidence based, and add canonical over-time proof so this cannot silently drift again.
28	
29	No production code was implemented for this plan.
30	
31	## Source Bug
32	
33	This plan is cross-linked with [pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-2026-06-02.md](./pinned-unpin-menu-and-degraded-health-2026-06-02.md).
34	
35	That bug doc established two client-side failures:
36	
37	- Pinned `Unpin` can appear and disappear because pinned rows render through a custom `UICollectionView` bridge that reloads during SwiftUI updates.
38	- System Health can mark Dock feed, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics degraded because a Dock row-window message (`Home: Showing 250 of 964`) is escalated into global connectivity partiality and then into per-category degradation.
39	
40	## Model Consensus
41	
42	Consensus artifact directory:
43	
44	`../../.arch_skill/model-consensus/codex-dock-pinned-health-architecture-20260602T122846Z/`
45	
46	Participants:
47	
48	- `Opus 4 8 Max` resolved as `claude-opus-4-8` with max effort.
49	- `GBD-55XI` resolved as `gpt-5.5` with xhigh effort.
50	
51	Both models independently converged on the same core fix:
52	
53	- Remove the duplicate pinned interaction path.
54	- Remove the overloaded `partial` meaning from host load state.
55	- Keep route diagnostics as the only owner of per-feature System Health degradation.
56	- Add proof that observes live updates over time, not only static snapshots.
57	
58	The main round-2 refinement was:
59	
60	- Prefer an explicit pinned reorder mode or sheet using native SwiftUI move behavior.
61	- Do not make custom inline drag reorder the first architecture, because that risks recreating a second gesture system on the same live row surface.
62	
63	## North Star
64	
65	The app should behave like this:
66	
67	- If a row is visible, the user can swipe it and use the same stable row actions whether the row is pinned or unpinned.
68	- Live Dock updates, layout updates, health ticks, and startup recovery do not close an action the user is actively trying to tap.
69	- A host can be online and still show only the first window of a large data set.
70	- `Showing 250 of 964` means "this view is windowed." It does not mean "the relay, thread detail, archive, voice, and diagnostics are degraded."
71	- System Health says `Degraded` only when it has direct route evidence or a true service failure signal.
72	- If route evidence has not been fetched yet, System Health says `Not checked` or `Checking`, not `Degraded`.
73	
74	## Architectural Principle
75	
76	One owner per fact:
77	
78	| Fact | Canonical owner | Current violation | Permanent fix |
79	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
80	| Row swipe action state | `DockSwipeActionRow` local SwiftUI state | Pinned rows use a separate UIKit collection/list path | Pinned and body rows use one SwiftUI row-action path |
81	| Pinned ordering | `DockStore.reorderPinnedRows` and `LocalMetadataEngine.reorderPinnedRows` | UIKit owns reorder gesture and normal pinned rendering | Dedicated SwiftUI reorder surface calls the existing reorder owner |
82	| Data-window completeness | Thread-card stream `complete`, `totalRows`, and `window` fields | Converted into `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` | Store as a window annotation on a loaded host state |
83	| Service degradation | Relay freshness and route diagnostics | Shares the same `partial` word as window completeness | Represent as a distinct degraded/offline/error status |
84	| Per-feature System Health | Route diagnostics from the relay/client observability path | Global partial fallback degrades every category | Categories degrade only from matching route evidence or true service failure |
85	| UI proof contract | `contract/proof/*.schema.json` plus the real producer | Producer/schema drift only appears during simulator dump | Fast producer-to-schema contract test plus live over-time UI proof |
86	
87	## Plan Part 1: One Dock Row Interaction Surface
88	
89	### Decision
90	
91	Pinned rows and body rows should render through the same SwiftUI row action component:
92	
93	- Keep `DockSwipeActionRow` as the row-action owner.
94	- Keep `DockView.dockRow(...)` / row content as the shared content path.
95	- Delete `DockPinnedReorderCollectionView`, `PinnedCollectionView`, its `Coordinator`, UIKit long-press recognizer, height-measurement loop, and normal pinned `UICollectionView` rendering.
96	
97	### Why
98	
99	The current pinned path uses `UICollectionView.reloadData()` during SwiftUI updates. UIKit reloads can close open swipe actions. That is the wrong architecture for a live-updating Dock surface.
100	
101	The correct architecture is not "reload more carefully." The correct architecture is that row actions have one owner, and that owner is stable across render updates unless the row identity or action state actually changes.
102	
103	### Reorder Decision
104	
105	Pinned reorder should move to a dedicated reorder surface:
106	
107	- Entry point: pinned section header action, for example `Reorder`.
108	- Surface: sheet or pushed screen, chosen by normal app UI conventions during implementation.
109	- Implementation direction: native SwiftUI move behavior, such as `List` with `EditMode` / `.onMove`.
110	- Commit path: call existing `DockStore.reorderPinnedRows(_:)`.
111	
112	Do not make inline drag-reorder on the normal live row surface the primary architecture. Inline drag would put swipe and reorder back into one gesture-arbitration surface, which is the class of problem this plan is removing.
113	
114	Do not keep UIKit behind a flag or as a fallback for normal pinned rendering. That would leave the side door open.
115	
116	### Owner Paths
117	
118	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockView.swift`
119	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockPinnedViews.swift`
120	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
121	- `CodexDock/Metadata/LocalMetadataEngine.swift`
122	
123	## Plan Part 2: Split Window Completeness From Health
124	
125	### Decision
126	
127	Replace the overloaded shared host status shape. The key architectural move is to remove `DockHostLoadStatus.partial(rowCount:message:)` rather than add more special cases around it.
128	
129	Target shape:
130	
131	```swift
132	public struct DockHostWindow: Equatable, Sendable {
133	    public let visibleRows: Int
134	    public let totalRows: Int
135	}
136	
137	public enum DockHostLoadStatus: Equatable, Sendable {
138	    case checking
139	    case loaded(rowCount: Int, window: DockHostWindow?)
140	    case empty
141	    case degraded(rowCount: Int, message: String)
142	    case offline(String)
143	    case error(String)
144	}
145	```
146	
147	The exact type and property names can move during implementation, but the semantic split should not:
148	
149	- `loaded(..., window:)` means the service is usable and the view is intentionally windowed.
150	- `degraded(...)` means the service path has a real problem but retained rows still exist.
151	- `offline` and `error` remain true unavailable states.
152	- `window` is display metadata. It is never connectivity evidence.
153	
154	Do not keep `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` as a compatibility alias. Removing it is valuable because the compiler forces every producer and consumer to declare which meaning it intended.
155	
156	### Why
157	
158	Right now `ThreadCardTable.hostStatus(...)` can return `.partial("Showing X of Y")` before freshness is consulted. That merges two unrelated facts:
159	
160	- data completeness: "the current view is only a window"
161	- health: "the service path is impaired"
162	
163	That overloaded value then flows into connectivity and System Health. The elegant fix is to sever the leak at the source, not string-match `Showing`.
164	
165	### Required Reclassification
166	
167	Every current `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` producer must be reclassified:
168	
169	- Fresh but windowed stream snapshot -> `.loaded(rowCount: visible, window: ...)`
170	- Stale heartbeat with retained rows -> `.degraded(rowCount: retained, message: ...)`
171	- Offline-with-cached rows -> `.degraded(rowCount: retained, message: ...)`
172	- Error-with-cached rows -> `.degraded(rowCount: retained, message: ...)`
173	- Refreshing/unknown transient with rows -> non-degrading checking or loaded state, depending on the actual freshness contract
174	
175	This split must live in the shared status type because Archive has the same status/phase pattern. A Dock-only workaround would leave the class of bug alive.
176	
177	### Owner Paths
178	
179	- `CodexDock/Dock/DockModels.swift`
180	- `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`
181	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
182	- `CodexDock/State/ArchiveStore.swift`
183	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockSharedViews.swift`
184	- `CodexDock/Features/Dock/DockGroupRows.swift`
185	- `CodexDock/Archive/ArchiveCleanupModels.swift`
186	
187	## Plan Part 3: Sever Completeness From Connectivity
188	
189	### Decision
190	
191	Connectivity rollups should never consume the `window` annotation.
192	
193	Fresh windowed data should map to online/loaded connectivity, while Dock still displays the window message.
194	
195	Only true service states should map into connectivity concern:
196	
197	- `.degraded` -> partial/degraded connectivity, if retained rows exist
198	- `.offline` -> offline connectivity
199	- `.error` -> error connectivity
200	- `.loaded(window:)` -> online connectivity
201	
202	`HostConnectivityPhase.partial` can still exist for true partial service availability. It must not mean "this view is windowed."
203	
204	### Why
205	
206	The repo currently has more than one connectivity rollup path:
207	
208	- `AppConnectivityStore`
209	- `ConnectivityDataEngine` / `ConnectivityRenderProjector`
210	
211	That duplication is a separate architectural smell, but this plan does not need to unify both rollups to fix the reported bug. Cutting the false signal upstream means both rollups receive the right fact.
212	
213	### Owner Paths
214	
215	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift`
216	- `CodexDock/Connectivity/ConnectivityDataEngine.swift`
217	- `CodexDock/Connectivity/ConnectivityRenderProjector.swift`
218	- `CodexDock/Runtime/ConnectivityEventSink.swift`
219	- `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`
220	- `CodexDock/State/ArchiveStore.swift`
221	
222	## Plan Part 4: Make System Health Evidence-Based
223	
224	### Decision
225	
226	System Health should use route diagnostics as the owner of per-feature health.
227	
228	Required behavior:
229	
230	- On open, automatically fetch route diagnostics through the existing diagnostics path.
231	- Debounce or skip the fetch if diagnostics are already fresh enough.
232	- While fetching, show `Checking`.
233	- If there is no route evidence yet, show `Not checked`.
234	- If route diagnostics fail to load, show a diagnostics fetch error or `Not checked` with clear action text.
235	- A category becomes `Degraded` only from matching route evidence or true service failure.
236	
237	Remove the fallback that turns global `.partial` into every category being `Degraded`.
238	
239	### Why
240	
241	Opening System Health is diagnostic intent. The user should not need to tap `Run check` before the screen can tell the truth. But the screen must also not invent degradation before evidence exists.
242	
243	The manual `Run check` action should remain as an explicit refresh.
244	
245	### Owner Paths
246	
247	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthView.swift`
248	- `CodexDock/Features/Status/SystemHealthProjector.swift`
249	- `CodexDock/State/AppConnectivityStore.swift`
250	- `CodexDock/Diagnostics/ObservabilityContract.swift`
251	
252	## Plan Part 5: Canonical Proof, Not Side Tests
253	
254	### Decision
255	
256	This class of bug needs proof that the app behaves correctly while updates happen over time. Static snapshot tests are not enough.
257	
258	Proof must live in canonical owner tests and proof-contract paths, not as one-off helper scripts.
259	
260	### Required Tests
261	
262	Fast Swift tests:
263	
264	- `DockStoreStreamTests`
265	  - fresh windowed snapshot is loaded with a window annotation, not partial/degraded
266	  - stale/offline/error retained-row cases become degraded
267	  - no `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` remains
268	- `ArchiveStore` tests
269	  - Archive uses the same status split and does not convert a fresh window into connectivity degradation
270	- `AppConnectivityStoreTests`
271	  - fresh windowed Dock and Archive hosts report online
272	  - true degraded retained-row hosts report partial/degraded connectivity
273	- `ConnectivityDataEngineTests`
274	  - runtime connectivity path agrees with `AppConnectivityStore`
275	- `SystemHealthProjectorTests`
276	  - route-less categories show `Not checked`, not `Degraded`
277	  - fresh windowed Dock status does not degrade thread detail, archive, voice, or diagnostics
278	  - true route degradation affects only the matching category
279	
280	UI and live-update proof:
281	
282	- `CodexDockUITests`
283	  - seed or pin multiple rows
284	  - relaunch the `iPhone 17` simulator
285	  - open a pinned row swipe action
286	  - inject or replay a Dock update
287	  - assert `Unpin` remains present and tappable across samples
288	- Existing over-time displayed UI harness
289	  - extend the canonical harness instead of adding a separate proof path
290	  - a skipped or hung dump is blocked, not green
291	
292	Proof contract:
293	
294	- `contract/proof/*.schema.json` remains the schema owner.
295	- Add a fast producer-to-schema test for the Swift displayed-state producer, including `DisplayedUIAppMetadata`.
296	- Decide once whether `configuredBuildNumber` belongs in the schema and make producer and schema agree.
297	- `rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'` should be trustworthy after the contract is fixed.
298	
299	### Required Commands
300	
301	Use the smallest relevant checks first:
302	
303	```bash
304	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreStreamTests
305	rtk swift test --filter AppConnectivityStoreTests
306	rtk swift test --filter ConnectivityDataEngineTests
307	rtk swift test --filter SystemHealthProjectorTests
308	rtk swift test --filter ArchiveScreenStoreTests
309	rtk swift test --filter ArchiveDataEngineTests
310	rtk swift test --filter ArchiveCleanupStoreTests
311	rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'
312	rtk make sim-ui-dump SIM='iPhone 17'
313	```
314	
315	If production relay code is not changed, `rtk npm run test:relay` is not required for this plan. If implementation touches relay DTO or contract code, run the relay tests too.
316	
317	## Implementation Phases
318	
319	These phases are intentionally ordered so each cut removes a class of ambiguity.
320	
321	### Phase 1: Shared Status Split
322	
323	- Introduce the window annotation type.
324	- Replace `DockHostLoadStatus.partial` with explicit loaded/degraded meanings.
325	- Update every producer and consumer until the compiler has no `partial` cases left for `DockHostLoadStatus`.
326	- Include Dock and Archive in the same cut.
327	
328	Done when:
329	
330	- Fresh windowed data is `loaded(window:)`.
331	- Retained-row service failures are `degraded`.
332	- No code can accidentally treat window completeness as health through `DockHostLoadStatus`.
333	
334	### Phase 2: Connectivity Mapping
335	
336	- Update Dock and Archive connectivity event production.
337	- Ensure both connectivity paths treat `loaded(window:)` as online.
338	- Keep true service degradation mapped to connectivity concern.
339	
340	Done when:
341	
342	- `Showing 250 of 964` can still render in Dock.
343	- The global connectivity indicator does not become partial solely because of that window.
344	
345	### Phase 3: System Health
346	
347	- Remove the global partial fallback that degrades every category.
348	- Fetch route diagnostics on open.
349	- Keep `Run check` as manual refresh.
350	- Render `Checking` / `Not checked` honestly while evidence is missing.
351	
352	Done when:
353	
354	- Route-less categories do not show copied Dock window text.
355	- Categories degrade only from route evidence or true service failure.
356	
357	### Phase 4: Pinned Row Surface
358	
359	- Render pinned rows through the same SwiftUI row-action path as body rows.
360	- Delete normal pinned `UICollectionView` rendering and the reload-driven UIKit bridge.
361	- Preserve pin/unpin persistence paths.
362	
363	Done when:
364	
365	- A pinned row and body row use the same swipe-action implementation.
366	- Live updates do not close the pinned row action just because the section re-rendered.
367	
368	### Phase 5: Reorder Surface
369	
370	- Add a dedicated pinned reorder surface using native SwiftUI move behavior.
371	- Commit order through `DockStore.reorderPinnedRows(_:)`.
372	- Do not restore UIKit or custom inline drag as a hidden fallback.
373	
374	Done when:
375	
376	- Pinned rows can be reordered without sharing the live swipe surface.
377	- Reorder has no path that can reload and close normal pinned row actions.
378	
379	### Phase 6: Canonical Proof
380	
381	- Add the fast unit tests listed above.
382	- Add the live pinned interaction-survival UI proof.
383	- Fix displayed UI producer/schema drift.
384	- Run the simulator proof paths.
385	
386	Done when:
387	
388	- A fresh windowed host proves online and non-degraded across unit and UI paths.
389	- Pinned `Unpin` survives an update in the actual `iPhone 17` simulator app.
390	- UI dump producer and schema cannot drift silently.
391	
392	## Rejected Alternatives
393	
394	Rejected because they preserve the bug class:
395	
396	- Keeping UIKit and making `reloadData()` smarter.
397	- Suppressing reloads only while a swipe is open.
398	- Pausing live Dock updates while a row action is open.
399	- Adding string checks for `Showing` in System Health.
400	- Fetching all rows so the Dock window message disappears.
401	- Using `partial(kind:)` as the health shape. The word `partial` is already overloaded; removing the word from host load status is cleaner.
402	- Building custom inline drag/swipe arbitration as the first reorder architecture.
403	- Leaving old UIKit reorder as a hidden fallback for testing or emergency use.
404	
405	## Non-Goals
406	
407	This plan does not:
408	
409	- Change relay status semantics.
410	- Make the iPhone connect directly to the raw app server.
411	- Query or control the physical iPhone 17 Pro.
412	- Implement production code.
413	- Rewrite the whole connectivity subsystem.
414	
415	The two connectivity rollup paths are a real follow-up risk. The consensus view is that severing the false signal at `DockHostLoadStatus` fixes the reported bug across both paths without expanding this plan into a broader rewrite.
416	
417	## Final Consensus Statement
418	
419	The elegant permanent solution is subtractive:
420	
421	- one row-action surface
422	- one reorder owner
423	- one typed meaning for data-window completeness
424	- one typed meaning for service degradation
425	- one evidence owner for System Health
426	- one canonical over-time proof path
427	
428	If this is implemented as specified, the current pinned unpin instability and false broad health degradation should be eliminated as an architectural class, not just patched at the observed symptoms.
429

5	    func testEngineAppliesRuntimeEventsAndProjectsOverallStatus() async throws {

62	    func testConnectivityScreenStoreDrainsRuntimeSinkDownstream() async throws {
63	        let host = makeHost()
64	        let registry = try HostRegistry(hosts: [host])
65	        let sink = ConnectivityEventSink()
66	        let appStore = AppConnectivityStore(registry: registry)
67	        let screenStore = ConnectivityScreenStore(
68	            registry: registry,
69	            eventSink: sink,

71	        )
72	
73	        screenStore.start(mirroring: appStore)
74	        await sink.record(
75	            ConnectivityRuntimeEvent(
76	                source: .dock,
77	                hostID: host.id,
78	                route: "dock/subscribe",
79	                status: "Loaded",
80	                phase: .online("Loaded"),
81	                recordedAt: Date(timeIntervalSince1970: 2_000)
82	            )
83	        )

85	        let snapshot = await waitForConnectivitySnapshot(in: screenStore)
86	        let appHosts = appStore.hosts
87

89	        XCTAssertEqual(appHosts.map(\.phase), [.online("Loaded")])
90	    }

92	    @MainActor
93	    private func waitForConnectivitySnapshot(
94	        in store: ConnectivityScreenStore,
95	        file: StaticString = #filePath,
96	        line: UInt = #line
97	    ) async -> ConnectivityRenderSnapshot? {
98	        for _ in 0..<50 {
99	            if store.snapshot.hosts.contains(where: { $0.phase == .online("Loaded") }) {
100	                return store.snapshot
101	            }
102	            try? await Task.sleep(for: .milliseconds(10))
103	        }
104	        XCTFail("Timed out waiting for connectivity snapshot", file: file, line: line)
105	        return nil
106	    }
107	}

1	import Foundation
2	
3	public struct LocalThreadMetadataKey: Codable, Equatable, Hashable, Sendable {
4	    public let hostID: String
5	    public let backendSessionID: String
6	    public let threadID: String
7	
8	    public init(hostID: String, backendSessionID: String, threadID: String) {
9	        self.hostID = hostID
10	        self.backendSessionID = backendSessionID
11	        self.threadID = threadID
12	    }
13	}
14	
15	public struct LocalThreadMetadata: Codable, Equatable, Sendable {
16	    // Local metadata decorates relay cards only. Pins, labels, and rails can be
17	    // local; title, status, activity, summary, freshness, and archive state must
18	    // come from the relay card stream.
19	    public var label: String? {
20	        didSet {
21	            label = Self.normalized(label)
22	        }
23	    }
24	    public var rail: DockRowRail?
25	    public var isPinned: Bool
26	    public var pinnedAt: Date?
27	    public var pinnedOrder: Int?
28	
29	    public init(
30	        label: String? = nil,
31	        rail: DockRowRail? = nil,
32	        isPinned: Bool = false,
33	        pinnedAt: Date? = nil,
34	        pinnedOrder: Int? = nil
35	    ) {
36	        self.label = Self.normalized(label)
37	        self.rail = rail
38	        self.isPinned = isPinned
39	        self.pinnedAt = isPinned ? pinnedAt : nil
40	        self.pinnedOrder = isPinned ? pinnedOrder : nil
41	    }
42	
43	    public var isEmpty: Bool {
44	        label == nil
45	            && rail == nil
46	            && !isPinned
47	            && pinnedAt == nil
48	            && pinnedOrder == nil
49	    }
50	
51	    private static func normalized(_ value: String?) -> String? {
52	        let trimmed = value?.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines)
53	        if let trimmed, !trimmed.isEmpty {
54	            return trimmed
55	        }
56	        return nil
57	    }
58	
59	    private enum CodingKeys: String, CodingKey {
60	        case label
61	        case rail
62	        case isPinned
63	        case pinnedAt
64	        case pinnedOrder
65	    }
66	
67	    public init(from decoder: Decoder) throws {
68	        let container = try decoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
69	        self.init(
70	            label: try container.decodeIfPresent(String.self, forKey: .label),
71	            rail: try container.decodeIfPresent(DockRowRail.self, forKey: .rail),
72	            isPinned: try container.decodeIfPresent(Bool.self, forKey: .isPinned) ?? false,
73	            pinnedAt: try container.decodeIfPresent(Date.self, forKey: .pinnedAt),
74	            pinnedOrder: try container.decodeIfPresent(Int.self, forKey: .pinnedOrder)
75	        )
76	    }
77	
78	    public func encode(to encoder: Encoder) throws {
79	        var container = encoder.container(keyedBy: CodingKeys.self)
80	        try container.encodeIfPresent(label, forKey: .label)
81	        try container.encodeIfPresent(rail, forKey: .rail)
82	        try container.encode(isPinned, forKey: .isPinned)
83	        try container.encodeIfPresent(pinnedAt, forKey: .pinnedAt)
84	        try container.encodeIfPresent(pinnedOrder, forKey: .pinnedOrder)
85	    }
86	}
87	
88	public protocol LocalThreadMetadataStoring: Sendable {
89	    func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
90	    func save(
91	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
92	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
93	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
94	    func save(
95	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
96	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
97	}
98	
99	public actor FileLocalThreadMetadataStore: LocalThreadMetadataStoring {
100	    private struct Entry: Codable {
101	        let key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
102	        let metadata: LocalThreadMetadata
103	    }
104	
105	    private let fileURL: URL
106	    private var cache: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]?
107	
108	    public init(fileURL: URL = FileLocalThreadMetadataStore.defaultFileURL()) {
109	        self.fileURL = fileURL
110	    }
111	
112	    public func load() async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
113	        if let cache {
114	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load cache hit entries=\(cache.count, privacy: .public)")
115	            return cache
116	        }
117	
118	        let loaded: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
119	        if FileManager.default.fileExists(atPath: fileURL.path) {
120	            DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load started path=\(self.fileURL.path, privacy: .public)")
121	            let data = try Data(contentsOf: fileURL)
122	            let entries = try JSONDecoder().decode([Entry].self, from: data)
123	            loaded = Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues: entries.map { ($0.key, $0.metadata) })
124	        } else {
125	            loaded = [:]
126	        }
127	        cache = loaded
128	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata load finished entries=\(loaded.count, privacy: .public)")
129	        return loaded
130	    }
131	
132	    public func save(
133	        _ metadata: LocalThreadMetadata?,
134	        for key: LocalThreadMetadataKey
135	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
136	        var values = try await load()
137	        if let metadata, !metadata.isEmpty {
138	            values[key] = metadata
139	        } else {
140	            values.removeValue(forKey: key)
141	        }
142	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist started host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(values.count, privacy: .public)")
143	        let persisted = try await save(values)
144	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata persist finished host_id=\(key.hostID, privacy: .public) thread_id=\(DockLog.publicID(key.threadID), privacy: .public) entries=\(persisted.count, privacy: .public)")
145	        return persisted
146	    }
147	
148	    public func save(
149	        _ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]
150	    ) async throws -> [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata] {
151	        let persistedValues = values.filter { !$0.value.isEmpty }
152	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist started entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
153	        try persist(persistedValues)
154	        cache = persistedValues
155	        DockLog.persistence.debug("thread metadata batch persist finished entries=\(persistedValues.count, privacy: .public)")
156	        return persistedValues
157	    }
158	
159	    private func persist(_ values: [LocalThreadMetadataKey: LocalThreadMetadata]) throws {
160	        try FileManager.default.createDirectory(
161	            at: fileURL.deletingLastPathComponent(),
162	            withIntermediateDirectories: true
163	        )
164	        let entries = values
165	            .map { Entry(key: $0.key, metadata: $0.value) }
166	            .sorted {
167	                [$0.key.hostID, $0.key.backendSessionID, $0.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
168	                    < [$1.key.hostID, $1.key.backendSessionID, $1.key.threadID].joined(separator: "\u{1f}")
169	            }
170	        let data = try JSONEncoder().encode(entries)
171	        try data.write(to: fileURL, options: [.atomic])
172	    }
173	
174	    public static func defaultFileURL() -> URL {
175	        let directory = FileManager.default.urls(
176	            for: .applicationSupportDirectory,
177	            in: .userDomainMask
178	        ).first ?? FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory
179	        return directory
180	            .appendingPathComponent("CodexDock", isDirectory: true)
181	            .appendingPathComponent("thread-metadata.json")
182	    }
183	}

3	struct ThreadDetailRenderProjector: Sendable {
4	    func render(
5	        snapshot: ThreadDetailSnapshot,
6	        requestCardPresentation: ThreadDetailRequestCardPresentation = ThreadDetailRequestCardPresentation(),
7	        options: ThreadDetailRenderOptions,
8	        revision: RenderRevision
9	    ) -> ThreadDetailRenderSnapshot {
10	        let filteredEvents = snapshot.events.filter { options.filter.includes($0) }
11	        let visibleEvents = Array(filteredEvents.prefix(options.visibleLimit))
12	        // Request cards are a decoration on canonical projection rows. Do not
13	        // pass or render a second card list that can drift from `snapshot.events`.
14	        let rows = visibleEvents.map { event in
15	            ThreadEventRenderRow(
16	                event: event,
17	                requestCard: requestCardPresentation.card(for: event)
18	            )
19	        }
20	
21	        return ThreadDetailRenderSnapshot(
22	            revision: revision,
23	            header: snapshot.header,
24	            liveState: snapshot.liveState,
25	            options: options,
26	            visibleWindow: ThreadVisibleWindow(
27	                startIndex: 0,
28	                rows: rows,
29	                totalMatchingCount: filteredEvents.count
30	            ),
31	            hasUnfilteredEvents: !snapshot.events.isEmpty
32	        )
33	    }
34	}

I have everything needed. The `dockCardID`/SessionRouter details are sufficiently traced. Let me compile the final evidence-backed report.

---

# Relay Identity Architecture — Evidence Report

All paths under `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client/`.

## Relevant relay files (glob result)
The relay is split across ~25 `scripts/dock-relay-*.mjs` modules. The identity-bearing ones are: `dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs`, `dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs`, `dock-relay-thread-detail-ledger.mjs`, `dock-relay-state-views.mjs`, `dock-relay-state-store.mjs`, `dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`, `dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs`, `dock-relay-thread-data.mjs`, `dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs`, and `dock-relay.mjs`.

---

## Q1 — ONE ENGINE OR MANY? → **One canonical engine; all identity strings are constructed in `dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs`.**

`dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs` is the sole module that CONSTRUCTS identity strings. It owns the segment grammar and every `projectionID*`/`sourceRef*`/`displayOrderKey` builder:

- `scripts/dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs:55-65` — segment primitives (`segment`, `hostSegment`, `threadSegment`).
- `:96-107` — `sourceRefForThreadItem` and `projectionIDForThreadItem`:
  ```js
  function projectionIDForThreadItem({ sourceHostID, threadID, turnID, itemID, rowRole }) {
    return `${sourceRefForThreadItem({ sourceHostID, threadID, turnID, itemID })}/${segment("row", rowRole)}`;
  }
  ```
- `:109-155` — `…ForThreadRequest`, `…ForThreadSystem`, `…ForThreadDiagnostic`, `…ForThreadCard`.
- `:79-94` — `threadDetailDisplayOrderKey`; `:177-188` — `threadCardDisplayOrderKey`.

Every other module only IMPORTS these:
- `dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:3-21` imports `projectionIDForThreadItem`, `sourceRefForThreadItem`, `threadDetailDisplayOrderKey`, etc., and re-exports the version constants. The adapter CALLS them (e.g. `:509`, `:675`, `:862-876`) but never builds an identity string by hand.
- `dock-relay-state-views.mjs:8-14` imports `projectionIDForThreadCard`, `sourceRefForThreadCard`, `threadCardDisplayOrderKey`; `normalizeThread` calls them at `:340-342`.
- `dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs:21` imports `projectionIDForThreadCard` and calls it for verification at `:3697`, `:3712`, `:4138`.

**One legacy exception that is dead code:** `dock-relay-state-views.mjs:70-74` still defines the old `host::thread` builder:
```js
function dockCardID(logicalHostID, threadID) {
  ...
  return hostID && id ? `${hostID}::${id}` : null;
}
```
It is exported (`:448`) but has **zero callers** anywhere in `scripts/` (grep for `dockCardID` returns only its definition/export plus consensus-artifact and bug-doc files). It is not used to build any emitted identity.

Verdict: **ONE engine.** No relay file builds its own competing identity strings on the live path.

---

## Q2 — DOCK/ARCHIVE STREAM SHAPE → **Legacy "card v2" grammar is GONE and actively forbidden. Dock card `id` is now `projectionID` (NOT `host::thread`).**

The Dock/Archive card id equals the engine `projectionID`, which is `host:<h>/thread:<t>/row:threadCard` — NOT `<logicalHostID>::<threadID>`:
- `dock-relay-state-views.mjs:340-356` (`normalizeThread`):
  ```js
  const projectionID = projectionIDForThreadCard({ sourceHostID, threadID });
  ...
  return {
    id: projectionID,
    ...
    projectionID,
    sourceRef,
    rowRole: "threadCard",
    displayOrderKey,
    logicalHostID: sourceHostID,   // present, but equals sourceHostID
    threadID,
    ...
  };
  ```
- The store ENFORCES this invariant: `dock-relay-state-store.mjs:96-101`: `if (card.id !== card.projectionID) throw …` and `if (card.logicalHostID !== card.sourceHostID) throw …` and `rowRole must be threadCard`.

Stream deltas/snapshots use the new grammar (`kind: upsert|delete|heartbeat`, `rows`, `projectionIDs`, `seq`, `epoch`, `view`, `viewParamsKey`, `order: "displayOrderKeyAscending"`):
- `dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs:89-128` (`cardDelta`) emits `rows` + `projectionIDs`, never `upsertCards`/`deleteCardIDs`.
- The delete path keys on `projectionID` (renamed `projectionIDs`), e.g. `dock-relay-state-store.mjs:649-651`, `727`.

The OLD card-v2 keys are explicitly rejected by the audit:
- `dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs:67-76`:
  ```js
  const FORBIDDEN_DOCK_STREAM_KEYS = new Set([
    "baseSeq", "stateGeneration", "cards", "cardIDs",
    "cardCount", "renderOrderCardIDs", "upsertCards", "deleteCardIDs",
  ]);
  ```
- Tests assert their absence: `dock-relay-state-subscriptions.test.mjs:67-68` (`"stateGeneration"`/`"baseSeq"` not present); `dock-relay-card-contract.test.mjs:357`.

`logicalHostID`, `cardsByID`, `stateGeneration`, `baseSeq` in source: `logicalHostID` survives only as a field that must equal `sourceHostID` (identity, but redundant — see Q4). `cardsByID` exists only as an **audit-side reconstruction Map** in `dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs` (`:659`, `:711`, `:772`…), keyed by `projectionID`, not as an emit shape.

**Contrast with Thread Detail ledger grammar:** the detail `projectionID` is finer-grained — `host:<h>/thread:<t>/turn:<turn>/item:<item>/row:<rowRole>` (`dock-relay-projection-engine.mjs:96-107`), whereas the Dock card is `host:<h>/thread:<t>/row:threadCard` (`:146-155`). Both share the identical segment grammar and the same `sourceRef` prefix; the thread card is effectively the thread-scoped truncation of the detail row identity.

---

## Q3 — LIVE vs CANONICAL IDENTITY → **YES. The relay HAS canonical `turnID` + `itemID` at live-notification time and computes the SAME canonical `projectionID` it would compute from `thread/turns/list` history. No temporary/pending identity is required.**

This is the central deliverable. Trace:

1. **Live notifications flow straight into the same ledger that processed history.** A per-session upstream client forwards every notification to `ThreadDetailLedger.applyNotification`:
   - `dock-relay.mjs:598-604` (`onNotification`) → `handleDetailNotification` → `dock-relay.mjs:517`: `detail.ledger.applyNotification(message)`.
   - That ledger was seeded from canonical history via `thread/read` + paged `thread/turns/list` (`dock-relay.mjs:368-385` `readThreadDetailLedger`; turns paged at `:340-365`).

2. **`item/started` / `item/completed` carry the canonical identity in `params`, and the engine reads it.** `dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:721-739`:
   ```js
   case "item/started":
   case "item/completed":
     ...
     return eventsFromItem(params.item, {
       sourceHostID, threadID: resolvedThreadID,
       liveParams: params,
       defaultMs: lifecycleActivityMs(message.method, params, nowMs),
       renderState: message.method === "item/completed" ? "settled" : "live",
     });
   ```
   Inside `eventsFromItem`, when `liveParams` is present the canonical IDs are resolved from the top-level notification params (with the item object as fallback) — `:450-471`:
   ```js
   const turnID = resolveIdentity("turnID", liveParams
     ? [ { value: liveParams.turnId }, { value: liveParams.turnID }, { value: liveParams.turn?.id },
         { value: item?.turnId }, { value: item?.turnID } ]
     : [ { value: turn?.id }, ... ]);
   const itemID = resolveIdentity("itemID", liveParams
     ? [ { value: liveParams.itemId }, { value: liveParams.itemID }, { value: item?.id } ]
     : [ { value: item?.id } ]);
   ```
   Then the **same** canonical builder is called — `:506-516`:
   ```js
   projectionID: projectionIDForItem({ sourceHostID, threadID, turnID: turnID.value, itemID: itemID.value, rowRole: spec.rowRole })
   ```
   This is byte-identical to the history path, because history items go through the **same** `eventsFromItem` (via `eventsFromTurn`, `:558-568`, with `turn` supplying the turnID and `item.id` the itemID).

3. **Deltas carry identity too.** `item/*/delta` handling reads `params.turnId`/`params.itemId` directly and builds the canonical item `projectionID` — `dock-relay-thread-detail-projection-adapter.mjs:647-681`:
   ```js
   const turnID = resolveIdentity("turnID", [{ value: params.turnId }, { value: params.turnID }]);
   const itemID = resolveIdentity("itemID", [{ value: params.itemId }, { value: params.itemID }]);
   ...
   projectionID: projectionIDForItem({ sourceHostID, threadID, turnID: turnID.value, itemID: itemID.value, rowRole: spec.rowRole })
   ```
   So a streaming delta upserts onto the exact same row id the completed item will use; `upsertRow` (`ledger:163-173`) appends streamed body onto the matching `projectionID`.

4. **Only the MISSING-identity case degrades — and it produces a diagnostic, not a pending-real-row.** If `turnId`/`itemId` are absent or conflict, `resolveIdentity` (`adapter:96-108`) returns `error`, and the code emits a `diagnosticEvent` (`:488-498`, `:725-731`) — an explicit "projection identity issue" row, not a temporary stand-in that later gets superseded by a different id.

**The one genuine "pending-then-resolve" mechanism is for server REQUESTS, not for live item identity.** `eventFromRequest` (`adapter:829-918`) uses a request-scoped id only when an item-backed identity is NOT available: `hasStableItemIdentity = Boolean(itemBackedProjection && turnID.value && itemID.value …)` (`:861`).
